## Changes on policy.nz since 23 October 2026

This archive captured the party's policy.nz policies on 23 October 2026; policy.nz is re-checked daily by [`tools/refresh_policies.py`](../../../tools/refresh_policies.py). Nothing is deleted: a policy that is no longer on policy.nz stays in this archive marked *withdrawn*. Full texts of new sources are archived separately; until then the links go to the original pages. Where this block and the sections below differ, this block is the newer text.

### New policies

#### Expand and simplify access to trades for secondary school students (POL55333)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that workforce shortages exist in key trade areas. Such professions are viable and positive pathways for many young people who are struggling to find jobs. Aligning education with labour market demands this party says, can be a long-term solution to improving employment outcomes. Additionally, the party argues that trades need to not be considered a second option.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would ensure that funding follows students so that schools receive funding for approved vocational-training programs that are done outside of the student's school. It would create 'Industry Awards' as a qualification equivalent to university entrance. This policy would allow for credits in approved courses to be counted, even after finishing high school.

Sources: ['ACT will put trades on an equal footing with university', 20 October 2026 (accessed 22 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-put-trades-on-an-equal-footing-with-university); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/act-party). Full text not yet archived.

#### Create a target of 10,000 children attending charter schools by 2029 (POL55347)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that parents and their children should have greater school choice. Charter schools can cater to specific needs, such as disability support or special athletic talent.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would set a target of 10,000 student enrolments by the end of 2029, with annual reporting on progress. It would reduce barriers relating to employment, property and funding for state and state-integrated schools to convert to charter schools. It would set a goal to have a charter school in every major town in New Zealand, paired with standards regarding funding and community demand.

Sources: ['Expanding Charter Schools', undated (accessed 23 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/expanding-charter-schools); ['ACT campaigning to transform 10,000 lives', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-campaigning-to-transform-10-000-lives); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/act-party). Full text not yet archived.

#### Allow more sheep to graze on conservation land (POL55348)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that taxpayers are currently funding a helicopter-spraying program. Instead, it says farmers should be allowed to graze their sheep on public conservation land to reduce pests and fire risk. The party claims that in the United States, Australia, and across Europe, targeted grazing is used as a tool for managing invasive plants, controlling vegetation growth, and reducing the risk of wildfires.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would give DOC explicit authority and direction to issue grazing licenses for specified areas of conservation land where grazing can be used effectively, as per an established ecological framework that would identify where grazing is appropriate. Licenses would be conditioned on compliance, and virtual fencing systems would be used to manage stock.

Sources: ['Grazing to Cut Pests and Fire Risk', undated (accessed 23 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/grazing); ['ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-drive-down-costs-for-farmers); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/act-party). Full text not yet archived.

#### Introduce new permitting standards for agriculture (POL55349)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that it wishes to expand accessibility and scope of permitting for agriculture. The party claims this can help promote growth and lower costs associated with regulatory compliance.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would introduce ten new permitting standards relating to farm plans, vegetable growing, on-farm water storage, gravel extraction, drain maintenance, effluent management, fertiliser application, farm quarries, wetland restoration, and small-and-medium-scale solar. It would additionally guarantee flexible land use, so farmers won’t require a resource consent when expanding into new markets if they remain compliant with national standards.

Sources: ['ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-drive-down-costs-for-farmers); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/act-party). Full text not yet archived.

#### Require compensation for individuals if council decisions affect private land (POL55350)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that private property rights are important to incentivise investment and to protect livelihoods. Councils can, through their policies regarding Significant Natural Areas or Outstanding Natural Landscapes, undermine property values and thus the investments of farmers.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would would require councils to pay 'fair' compensation if decisions made by such councils interfere with agricultural industry and farming.

Sources: ['ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-drive-down-costs-for-farmers); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/act-party). Full text not yet archived.

#### Create a rural workforce visa (POL55353)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that rural workforce visas are seasonal, such as the Global Workforce Seasonal Visa and the Peak Seasonal Visa. The party says a year-round visa needs to be introduced to ensure labour demands are met.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would create a standalone, three-year visa specifically for dairy, sheep and beef, and general farm work. Would be tied to industry, not location or employer. The visa would be for 3 years, if no suitable New Zealander is available, the visa is reissued for a further three years. The party would additionally add a new agricultural stream to the Work to Residence Visa.

Sources: ['A Rural Workforce Visa', undated (accessed 24 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/rural-visa); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/act-party). Full text not yet archived.

#### Reduce regulations related to selling home-kill meat (POL55362)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that it could potentially be cheaper for consumers to buy an animal directly from a producer, rather than once it has been processed by a butcher. It says buying and processing home kill should be easier. It says that currently, home-killed meat can only be eaten the animal owner, their family or household, and farm employees and that the rules haven't been updated in twenty years.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would revise regulations around selling and purchasing home-kill meat.

Sources: ['Cutting red tape between the farm gate and the freezer', 31 August 2026 (accessed 26 October 2026)](https://www.beehive.govt.nz/release/cutting-red-tape-between-farm-gate-and-freezer); ['ACT will make farming fun again ', 20 September 2026 (accessed 21 September 2026)]( /web/20260920235739/https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-make-farming-fun-again); ['ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-drive-down-costs-for-farmers); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/act-party). Full text not yet archived.

### Updated policies

#### Remove some rules around pharmacy locations, ownership and licences (POL54643)

_Updated on policy.nz, seen 28 October 2026: sources._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that removing the rule that prevents a single person or entity from owning more than five pharmacies would make it easier to open new pharmacies. Changing other rules about pharmacy locations, licenses and qualifications for pharmacists would make it easier to open and staff pharmacies anywhere in the country.

**How** (*policy.nz*): The party would change regulatory settings to implement the reforms. Online prescription e-lockers can be used to help those in rural areas access medication when pharmacies may have limited opening hours.

Sources: ['Your pharmacist should be your first stop', 6 August 2026 (accessed 06 August 2026)](documents/news-your-pharmacist-should-be-your-first-stop.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/news/your-pharmacist-should-be-your-first-stop)); [Let Pharmacies Do More](documents/let-pharmacies-do-more.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/let-pharmacies-do-more)); [Pharmacy First](documents/pdf-policy-pharmacy-02.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/actnz/pages/36340/attachments/original/1787116582/policy_pharmacy_02.pdf?1787116582)); ['ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-drive-down-costs-for-farmers)

#### Increase the areas of conservation land which can be accessed by helicopter for hunting (POL54646)

_Updated on policy.nz, seen 28 October 2026: sources._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that in areas of forest and mountains where people want to hunt, there are "no-fly" and "no-landing" areas for helicopters with no clear reasoning. In areas where helicopters are the fastest way in, access restrictions should be justified with obvious safety or conservation reasons.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would allow the Game Council to designate helicopter landing sites, and restrict commercial venison operators by animal gender when necessary, leaving trophy stags for hunters. DOC would be required to use public tests to designate where aircraft could land, and would not have any say in which types of helicopters were used. The Outdoors Access Commission would be asked to make hunting access a priority in its work programme.

Sources: ['Open the Backcountry', undated (accessed 07 August 2026)](documents/open-the-backcountry.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/open-the-backcountry)); [Backing Hunters](documents/pdf-policy-backing-hunters-02-2.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/actnz/pages/36342/attachments/original/1787117027/policy_backing_hunters_02-2.pdf?1787117027)); ['ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-drive-down-costs-for-farmers)

#### Make disrupting lawful hunters with drones or by standing in the line of fire an offence (POL54672)

_Updated on policy.nz, seen 28 October 2026: sources._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that people can disrupt hunters by stepping into the line of fire, or disturbing game birds with a drone. This should not happen if a hunter is following legal guidelines and safety protocols. While people are free to protest hunting, those protests should not place anyone at risk.  It says that currently there are no laws covering this situation which needs to change.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would create specific infringement offences for standing in the line of fire of a hunter, and for disturbing game birds with aircraft like drones or helicopters. These infringements would not apply if the hunter was not following the relevant laws and guidelines.

Sources: ['Protect Lawful Hunting', undated (accessed 07 August 2026)](documents/protect-lawful-hunting.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/protect-lawful-hunting)); [Backing Hunters](documents/pdf-policy-backing-hunters-02-2.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/actnz/pages/36342/attachments/original/1787117027/policy_backing_hunters_02-2.pdf?1787117027)); ['ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-drive-down-costs-for-farmers)

#### Give the Game Council responsibility for game animals on conservation land (POL54674)

_Updated on policy.nz, seen 28 October 2026: sources._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that legislation currently treats deer as pest animals to be exterminated rather than game animals to be hunted. The Game Council can advise DOC but does not make decisions. Hunters spend time in the area where these animals live and should be making decisions about what happens to game animals on conservation land.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would transfer responsibility for game animals from DOC to the Game Council. It would also give the Council more funding to recognise its further responsibilities.

Sources: ['Hunter-led Game Management', undated (accessed 07 August 2026)](documents/game-management.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/game-management)); [Backing Hunters](documents/pdf-policy-backing-hunters-02-2.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/actnz/pages/36342/attachments/original/1787117027/policy_backing_hunters_02-2.pdf?1787117027)); ['ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-drive-down-costs-for-farmers)

#### Give volunteer groups more opportunities and funding for maintenance on conservation land (POL54678)

_Updated on policy.nz, seen 28 October 2026: sources._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that that DOC has a 30 percent maintenance shortfall and has issued more than 2,300 closure alerts since 2021. Volunteer groups carry out track and hut maintenance, but should receive funding for this over multiple years rather than applying annually. Creating a system for groups to receive biodiversity credits will incentivise further volunteer work in the hills.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would require DOC to give community groups the first opportunity for funding for maintenance on conservation land. Community groups would be allowed to sign multi-year contracts for work they are able to do. If biodiversity benefits were independently verified, groups including hunters would receive biodiversity credits. The Game Council and Deerstalkers Association would be formally represented when deciding how animals on conservation land were managed.

Sources: ['Back the Volunteers', undated (accessed 07 August 2026)](documents/back-the-volunteers.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/back-the-volunteers)); [Backing Hunters](documents/pdf-policy-backing-hunters-02-2.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/actnz/pages/36342/attachments/original/1787117027/policy_backing_hunters_02-2.pdf?1787117027)); ['ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-drive-down-costs-for-farmers)

#### Expand rural policing (POL54894)

_Updated on policy.nz, seen 28 October 2026: sources._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that there is a lack of reporting of rural crime in NZ. It attributes this to a lack of trust in whether police will investigate. The prosecution rate is presently at 15%.  The lack of enforcement encourages rural crime.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would provide additional funding to expand the 111 service and hire more officers for rural areas, with a target of an additional 100,000 extra patrol hours each year. It would establish a dedicated rural crime unit.

Sources: ['Rural Crime Crackdown', undated (accessed 07 August 2026)](documents/rural-crime.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/rural-crime)); ['ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-drive-down-costs-for-farmers)

#### Repeal the Zero Carbon Act and NZ's net zero goal (POL55046)

_Updated on policy.nz, seen 28 October 2026: sources._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that NZ should play its part to reduce emissions but only in line with what other trading partners do, so that the country is not at a competitive disadvantage. The net zero target is arbitrary, and emissions reductions should be weighted in terms of trade.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would repeal the current Zero Carbon Act and adopted a trade-weighted approach to emissions reduction instead. The net zero by 2050 goal would be removed, and New Zealand would only do what its trading partners are doing.  This party would also protect NZ workers at risk of losing their jobs in high-emissions industries like steel production, so that these industries face lower carbon prices or none at all and are not at a competitive disadvantage.

Sources: ['Scrap Net Zero, Cut the Carbon Tax' (PDF), 6 September 2026 (accessed 07 September 2026)](documents/pdf-scrap-net-zero-policy-09.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/actnz/pages/37031/attachments/original/1788642905/Scrap_Net_Zero_policy_09.pdf?1788642905)); ['ACT will make farming fun again ', 20 September 2026 (accessed 21 September 2026)](documents/news-act-will-make-farming-fun-again.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-make-farming-fun-again)); [Scrap Net Zero, Cut the Carbon Tax](documents/scrap-net-zero-cut-the-carbon-tax.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/scrap-net-zero-cut-the-carbon-tax)); [Make Farming Fun Again](documents/make-farming-fun-again.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/make-farming-fun-again)); [ACT’s Plan to Make Farming Fun Again](documents/pdf-acts-plan-to-make-farming-fun-again.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/actnz/pages/37460/attachments/original/1789711573/ACT's_plan_to_Make_Farming_Fun_Again.pdf?1789711573)); ['ACT will make farming fun again ', 20 September 2026 (accessed 21 September 2026)]( /web/20260920235739/https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-make-farming-fun-again); ['ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-drive-down-costs-for-farmers)

#### Remove the carbon price floor and return ETS profits to households (POL55047)

_Updated on policy.nz, seen 28 October 2026: sources._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that the Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS) acts as a "carbon tax", with a minimum price for carbon credits set by the government. This means the auctions do not work properly and raises the price of goods and services. The supply of carbon credits should be increased and the profit returned as a refund to New Zealanders.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would remove the price floor from the Emissions Trading Scheme to place downward pressure on the carbon price. 100 percent of the money from the carbon auction would be returned to New Zealanders as a tax refund. If the amount became so low that the refund was impractical to deliver, it would mean prices had fallen so that people had lower prices for goods and services and would no longer need the tax refund.  Conversions of farmland to permanent forest for creating carbon credits would be discouraged.

Sources: ['Scrap Net Zero, Cut the Carbon Tax' (PDF), 6 September 2026 (accessed 07 September 2026)](documents/pdf-scrap-net-zero-policy-09.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/actnz/pages/37031/attachments/original/1788642905/Scrap_Net_Zero_policy_09.pdf?1788642905)); [Scrap Net Zero, Cut the Carbon Tax](documents/scrap-net-zero-cut-the-carbon-tax.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/scrap-net-zero-cut-the-carbon-tax)); ['ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-drive-down-costs-for-farmers)

#### Reduce emissions with a focus on new technology (POL55048)

_Updated on policy.nz, seen 28 October 2026: sources._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that many of the changes required to reduce emissions can be provided by novel technology rather than the emissions trading scheme or similar financial systems. To protect prosperity, it says there should be fewer barriers for people to invest in new technologies, especially those which may reduce emissions.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would continue to oppose any new financial penalties for carbon emissions. It would remove regulations that it says prevent people from investing in new technology with potential emission-reduction benefits.

Sources: ['Scrap Net Zero, Cut the Carbon Tax' (PDF), 6 September 2026 (accessed 07 September 2026)](documents/pdf-scrap-net-zero-policy-09.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/actnz/pages/37031/attachments/original/1788642905/Scrap_Net_Zero_policy_09.pdf?1788642905)); ['ACT will make farming fun again ', 20 September 2026 (accessed 21 September 2026)](documents/news-act-will-make-farming-fun-again.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-make-farming-fun-again)); [Scrap Net Zero, Cut the Carbon Tax](documents/scrap-net-zero-cut-the-carbon-tax.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/scrap-net-zero-cut-the-carbon-tax)); [Make Farming Fun Again](documents/make-farming-fun-again.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/make-farming-fun-again)); [ACT’s Plan to Make Farming Fun Again](documents/pdf-acts-plan-to-make-farming-fun-again.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/actnz/pages/37460/attachments/original/1789711573/ACT's_plan_to_Make_Farming_Fun_Again.pdf?1789711573)); ['ACT will make farming fun again ', 20 September 2026 (accessed 21 September 2026)]( /web/20260920235739/https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-make-farming-fun-again); ['ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-drive-down-costs-for-farmers)

#### Ensure agriculture is not included in emission reduction programmes (POL55054)

_Updated on policy.nz, seen 28 October 2026: sources._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that emissions-focused regulation worries farmers who are concerned with industry competitiveness in global export markets. The party argues that the government is getting in the way of decisions that should be made by farmers, and that they should be supported in leading environmental protections, since they have a vested interest in the preservation of their land.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would omit agriculture from climate-related legislation such as the Zero Carbon Act and Emissions Trading Scheme. The party has supported reforms to the Resource Management Act, shifting funding from Te Mana o te Wai to rural catchment groups, increasing funding for rural catchment groups, allowing targeted grazing on suitable DOC land, and continuing the war against wilding pines.

Sources: ['ACT will make farming fun again ', 20 September 2026 (accessed 21 September 2026)](documents/news-act-will-make-farming-fun-again.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-make-farming-fun-again)); [Make Farming Fun Again](documents/make-farming-fun-again.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/make-farming-fun-again)); [ACT’s Plan to Make Farming Fun Again](documents/pdf-acts-plan-to-make-farming-fun-again.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/actnz/pages/37460/attachments/original/1789711573/ACT's_plan_to_Make_Farming_Fun_Again.pdf?1789711573)); ['ACT will make farming fun again ', 20 September 2026 (accessed 21 September 2026)]( /web/20260920235739/https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-make-farming-fun-again); ['ACT will drive down costs for farmers', 22 October 2026 (accessed 23 October 2026)](https://www.act.org.nz/news/act-will-drive-down-costs-for-farmers)

#### Remove the "six months" caveat for assisted dying (POL55161)

_Updated on policy.nz, seen 28 October 2026: sources._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that since 2021, New Zealanders have had the option of assisted dying, and the Ministry of Health's first statutory review recommended 25 changes to the law. ACT released its **[ACT Fiscal Plan 2026](documents/pdf-act-2026-fiscal-plan.md)** (12-page PDF, 11 October 2026; [original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/actnz/pages/38747/attachments/original/1791599898/ACT_2026_Fiscal_Plan.pdf?1791599898)), with a landing page ([fiscalplan](documents/fiscalplan.md)) and an interactive debt microsite ([balancethebooks.nz](documents/fiscal-plan.md)). Key figures as stated in the PDF (all figures are ACT's; $ nominal):

- **Debt:** net core Crown debt (excluding NZ Super Fund) of $217 billion by June 2031, which ACT says is $12.4 billion lower than current Treasury forecasts (the PDF's "Headline Figures" page also describes it as "$12 billion lower than forecast in the Pre-election Fiscal Update"; the costing table shows 217.336 vs 229.769).
- **Operating balance:** OBEGAL surplus of $13.6 billion in 2030/31 (vs $8.9 billion under current Government plans); OBEGALx $16.4 billion (vs $11.7 billion); OBEGALx in small surplus in 2027/28, a year earlier than current plans; OBEGAL returns to a $5.1 billion surplus in 2028/29.
- **No new taxes; no broad-based tax cuts in this plan** — "several strategic tax cuts" instead: no tax on KiwiSaver earnings ($1.065bn in 2027/28 rising to $1.437bn in 2030/31), a Carbon Tax Refund (est. ~$100 per household), an uncapped donation tax credit, reformed crypto tax treatment, and $264m of targeted tax relief "to be announced".
- **New operating spending (outside the operating allowance), $445m in 2027/28 rising to $551m:** expanded pharmacy minor-ailments scheme, Local Tourism Dividend, Young Investors Fund (~$35m/yr, $500 for Year 11 students), Overstayers Investigation Unit ($60m/yr), rural crime funding, electronic money management for long-term Jobseeker recipients, Three Strikes for Burglary, Working with Children Check, independent school subsidy indexation, and a $100m/yr initiative "to be announced".
- **Savings:** future operating allowances cut from $2.4bn to $2bn a year (+$0.4bn in 2027/28 rising to +$1.6bn in 2030/31); non-welfare, non-frontline spending returned to 2017 levels per person (headline reductions $1.5bn in 2027/28, $2.8bn, $3.2bn, $2.4bn in 2030/31 — including abolishing demographic ministries ~$187m/yr and cutting foreign aid to 2017 levels excluding Ukraine ~$283m/yr); NZ Super age rising by three months a year to 67 by 2035 ($0.46bn rising to $1.89bn, less compassionate early access); five-year benefit stand-down for residence-class visa holders; tighter medical certification for health/disability benefits; replacing the KiwiSaver Government Contribution ($0.52–0.59bn/yr); lower financing costs ($452m by 2030/31).
- **Capital/non-operating:** $2m for anti-social noise cameras; $2bn contingency for a National Cancer Centre; $150m contingency for a new Epsom secondary school; maintain the suspension of NZ Super Fund contributions.

### Make the abuse of a companion animal in a family violence situation a crime (POL54651)

***Key policy** (policy.nz) · Topics: community-and-inclusion, law-justice-and-government, animal-welfare, women, family-justice-and-safety, key-policies-community-and-inclusion · Summary: policy.nz*

**Statement:** Make the abuse of a companion animal in a family violence situation a crime

**Why:** This party says that pets are being threatened and abused to coerce people in family violence situations and prevent them from leaving. Research shows half of victims delay leaving a violent situation because they are concerned about their pets. Criminalising the abuse of animals in this context will give Police more tools to protect victims. States in Australia and the US have enacted similar laws and New Zealand needs to do the same.

**How:** This party would amend the Crimes Act to make abusing a pet with the goal of coercion an offence punishable by a maximum seven years in prison. Protection orders would be strengthened to ensure offenders cannot control access to a pet and ensure pets are not left with abusers. Police would be required to record the presence of pets in a family violence situation and receive clear operational guidance around removing pets to a safe place if the animal is at risk of harm.

**Statement:** Remove the carbon price floor and return ETS profits to households

**Why:** This party says that the Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS) acts as a "carbon tax", with a minimum price for carbon credits set by the government. **Statement:** Limit the number of branded items in school uniforms to reduce costs

**Why:** This party says that in 2025, 38,000 WINZ hardship loans were issued to help families cover the cost of school uniforms, and in some cases the combined cost for school uniforms is over $1,000. Limiting state schools to just three branded school items will make uniforms more affordable for New Zealanders. Generic items such as socks would be available from low-cost retailers like The Warehouse or KMart. School uniforms can promote school culture but expensive uniforms don't improve educational outcomes, and similar policies in parts of Australia and the UK have been successful.

**How:** This party would limit state schools to three mandatory branded items as part of a uniform. Alternative, generic options for clothes like skirts, shirts, trousers and socks could be selected from low-cost retail stores. This policy would only apply to everyday items worn to school, not to more special items like branded clothing for sports teams.

### Count carbon dioxide and methane differently under emissions targets (POL54667)

*Topics: environment, economy, emissions-reduction, agriculture, climate-adaptation · Summary: policy.nz*

**Statement:** Count carbon dioxide and methane differently under emissions targets

**Why:** This party says that carbon dioxide and methane both contribute to global heating. Carbon dioxide stays in the atmosphere longer than methane, which is largely produced by the dairy and sheep industries.

**How:** This party would rewrite NZ's Nationally Determined Contributions plan, which is required by the Paris Agreement. It would differentiate between the emissions caused by methane and carbon dioxide so that methane emissions do not have to be reduced by the same degree as carbon emissions. A "split gas approach" would calculate the emissions generated by carbon dioxide and methane differently. Carbon dioxide emissions would be reduced while methane levels could continue at current levels.

### Exclude purely spiritual and religious effects from infrastructure planning law (POL55191)

*Topics: te-ao-maori, transport-and-infrastructure, te-reo-maori-and-culture, infrastructure-funding-and-planning · Summary: policy.nz*

**Statement:** Exclude purely spiritual and religious effects from infrastructure planning law

**Why:** This party says that spiritual beliefs, particularly those that come from Te Ao Māori, should not be used as the basis for assessing an infrastructure project's viability. It says that planning law should regulate effects that can be identified, measured and tested, and protect rights recognised by law. It should not require planners, councils or judges to rule on spiritual or religious beliefs.

**How:** This party would exclude purely spiritual and religious effects. It would legislate that a religious or spiritual belief, or a claim of spiritual harm, could not on its own be treated as an adverse effect or justify refusing or restricting consent, requesting further information, or imposing a consent condition. The rule would apply equally to all religions and belief systems and use the test already applied under the Marine and Coastal Area (Takutai Moana) Act. It would also ban compulsory spiritual observances. No consent or permit could require anyone to perform, take part in, arrange or fund a prayer, karakia, blessing or other religious observance. Anyone who wants to do these things voluntarily could still do so.

**Full text:**

### Focus National Land Transport Fund on road infrastructure only (POL54974)

***Key policy** (policy.nz) · Topics: transport-and-infrastructure, public-transport-cycling-and-walking, cars-and-roads, infrastructure-funding-and-planning, key-policies-transport-and-infrastructure · Summary: policy.nz*

**Statement:** Focus National Land Transport Fund on road infrastructure only

**Why:** This party says infrastructure should have its funding protected so that governments cannot redirect its revenue for other purposes. People have paid the fuel tax expecting it to fund the road infrastructure they use, as opposed to other priorities. Mana Whenua considerations, non-functional art, monuments, and decorative amenities on roads should also be excluded for this same reason.

**How:** This party would legislate that the National Land Transport Fund be used only for road-related infrastructure. The party would also amend procurement rules to not favour any group over another.

### Require infrastructure projects to consider a cheaper option (POL54975)

***Key policy** (policy.nz) · Topics: transport-and-infrastructure, cars-and-roads, public-transport-cycling-and-walking, infrastructure-funding-and-planning, key-policies-transport-and-infrastructure · Summary: policy.nz*

**Statement:** Require infrastructure projects to consider a cheaper option

**Why:** This party says that potential infrastructure projects, when seeking approval, should be required to publish a lowest-cost safe option alongside the preferred option. Both options should include cost, delivery time, and benefit-cost ratio for each. The party says this is to assess whether the preferred design is taking unnecessary steps or being made with overly conservative assumptions.

**How:** This party would mandate affordability and efficacy standards, made through the comparison with a cheaper alternative design, be applied to all infrastructure projects seeking government approval.

### Introduce an affordability test on used-car import regulations (POL54977)

*Topics: transport-and-infrastructure, incomes-and-employment, cars-and-roads, prices · Summary: policy.nz*

**Statement:** Introduce an affordability test on used-car import regulations

**Why:** This party says that regulations for used cars being imported into NZ can push up costs for people and families needing to buy a car. Import passenger registrations have fallen from around 165,000 in 2017 to 85,000 as people increasingly keep their current car for longer, putting off upgrading to newer, safer models.

### Encourage people generating power to sell it to the grid (POL55162)

*Topics: incomes-and-employment, transport-and-infrastructure, prices, energy · Summary: policy.nz*

**Statement:** Encourage people generating power to sell it to the grid

**Why:** This party says that there's a lack of competition in the energy sector. However, independent analysis commissioned by the government found no material competition problem requiring the break-up of the major generator-retailers. Instead, the party says regulatory barriers are the key driver of the cost of power. Encouraging people to sell excess power would reward people who invest their own money in generation and storage.

**How:** This party would allow people with excess power, often from solar installed on their house, to sell their excess power. The selling of excess power would be done by businesses and community energy schemes, subject to appropriate metering, network charging and consumer protections.

*Topics: transport-and-infrastructure, economy, urban-planning-and-resource-management, energy, economic-development-and-industry, oil-gas-and-mining · Summary: policy.nz*

**Statement:** Establish a statutory body to ensure compensation for investors in mineral extraction

**Why:** This party says that New Zealand needs to produce energy through mineral extraction. Extraction takes a long time between the initial investment and the returns, and investors need confidence that consent process will remain in place.

**How:** This party would establish a statutory body to ensure compensation for investors in mineral extraction. It would facilitate this by adding property rights into the New Zealand Bill of Rights Act and ensuring that any legal challenge opposing a permit does not suspend that permit.

parties/alliance/policies/README.md:
# Alliance Party of Aotearoa New Zealand — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **Alliance Party of Aotearoa New Zealand** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **27 policies** listed, backed by **37 full-text source documents**.

- Party website: <https://allianceparty.nz/>
- Registration: 5 August 2026 (re-registered; Electoral Commission register)

## About this list

The relaunched Alliance (leader Victor Billot) released its 2026 platform as a series of policy announcements (September–October 2026), each with a full policy PDF: tax and costings, workers' rights, environment, health, transport, social security, gender equality, small business, justice, child poverty, housing, retirement, Te Tiriti and constitution, trade, public ownership, and foreign affairs and defence. All 17 PDFs and all policy posts are captured. The main commitments of each document are listed below.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/alliance/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). Party claims (costs, statistics) are reported as the party's claims, not verified.

**Gaps and caveats.** Only the tax package has a separate costing document. Policy PDFs were extracted with pdftotext (page numbers kept). Earlier 2026 posts responding to news are captured where they state policy (Universal Child Benefit, conference).

## Headline policies

- [Make the first $20,000 of everyone's income tax-free](#make-the-first-20000-of-everyones-income-tax-free-all-01) — Incomes & employment
- [Introduce a 2.5% annual wealth tax on net wealth over $2 million, with a trust tax](#introduce-a-25-annual-wealth-tax-on-net-wealth-over-2-million-with-a-trust-tax-all-02) — Incomes & employment
- [Make full employment a central goal, with a 35-hour week and five weeks' annual leave](#make-full-employment-a-central-goal-with-a-35-hour-week-and-five-weeks-annual-leave-all-05) — Incomes & employment
- [Provide 52 weeks' paid parental leave for all workers and paid compassionate leave](#provide-52-weeks-paid-parental-leave-for-all-workers-and-paid-compassionate-leave-all-07) — Incomes & employment
- [Put all electricity generation, transmission, distribution and retail into full public ownership](#put-all-electricity-generation-transmission-distribution-and-retail-into-full-public-ownership-all-09) — Transport & infrastructure
- [Create a public Community Health Service with free GP, dental, optical, audiology and mental-health care](#create-a-public-community-health-service-with-free-gp-dental-optical-audiology-and-mental-health-care-all-13) — Health
- [Introduce a Universal Benefit and abolish benefit sanctions, stand-downs and beneficiary debt](#introduce-a-universal-benefit-and-abolish-benefit-sanctions-stand-downs-and-beneficiary-debt-all-16) — Incomes & employment
- [Restore a Universal Child Benefit paid to every child's main carer, plus a Universal Early Years Benefit for under-threes](#restore-a-universal-child-benefit-paid-to-every-childs-main-carer-plus-a-universal-early-years-benefit-for-under-threes-all-17) — Incomes & employment
- ['Three strikes and into treatment': rehabilitation-focused justice with no private prisons](#three-strikes-and-into-treatment-rehabilitation-focused-justice-with-no-private-prisons-all-21) — Law, justice & government
- [Clear the social housing waitlist in five years through a national state-house rebuilding programme](#clear-the-social-housing-waitlist-in-five-years-through-a-national-state-house-rebuilding-programme-all-22) — Housing
- [Keep NZ Super at 65, raise the married rate to 72.5% of the after-tax average wage, and end means-testing for long-term aged care](#keep-nz-super-at-65-raise-the-married-rate-to-725-of-the-after-tax-average-wage-and-end-means-testing-for-long-term-aged-care-all-23) — Incomes & employment
- [Make New Zealand non-aligned, restructure defence for peacekeeping and disaster response, and review foreign military and intelligence facilities](#make-new-zealand-non-aligned-restructure-defence-for-peacekeeping-and-disaster-response-and-review-foreign-military-and-intelligence-facilities-all-27) — Defence & foreign affairs

## Community & inclusion

### Guarantee free, accessible abortion and contraception and require gender-impact assessment of government decisions (ALL-19)

**How** (*archive*): A Gender Audit framework, a Pay Equity Bureau, secure non-contestable funding for women's refuges, affordable high-quality childcare, and support for informed-consent gender-affirming care.

Full text: [Women, Gender Equality, and Economic Security (PDF)](documents/pdf-women-gender-equality-economic-security-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-women-gender-equality-economic-security-policy-2026.pdf)); [52 Weeks’ Paid Parental Leave in Our Gender Equality Plan](documents/post-2026-09-16-alliance-52-weeks-paid-parental-leave-gender-equal.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-52-weeks-paid-parental-leave-gender-equality/))

## Defence & foreign affairs

### Refuse trade deals with investor–state dispute settlement and seek to remove it from existing deals (ALL-25)

**How** (*archive*): Trade policy that protects jobs, public services and the ability to regulate; retain tariffs as a sparing option; Māori consent on agreements affecting Māori interests; stronger buy-local procurement.

Full text: [Alliance Trade Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-trade-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-trade-policy-2026.pdf)); [Open, Not Owned: Alliance Party Announces Trade Policy](documents/post-2026-09-28-open-not-owned-alliance-trade-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/open-not-owned-alliance-trade-policy/))

### Make New Zealand non-aligned, restructure defence for peacekeeping and disaster response, and review foreign military and intelligence facilities (ALL-27)

**How** (*archive*): Withdraw from inconsistent military alliances, remove offensive capabilities, strengthen the nuclear-free Pacific, support Palestinian self-determination and right of return, cancel unsustainable Global South debt, raise aid toward 0.7% of GNI and ease Pacific migration barriers.

Full text: [Alliance Foreign Affairs, Defence and International Relations Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-foreign-affairs-defence-international-relations-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/alliance-foreign-affairs-defence-international-relations-policy-2026.pdf)); [A Commitment to Peace: Alliance Party Releases Foreign Affairs, Defence, and International Relations Policy](documents/post-2026-10-04-alliance-foreign-affairs-defence-international-rel.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-foreign-affairs-defence-international-relations-policy/))

## Economy

### Introduce a 0.1% financial transactions levy on equity and foreign-exchange turnover (ALL-04)

**How** (*archive*): Estimated at $0.64bn a year; wages, rent and mortgage payments, household bills and KiwiSaver contributions are excluded.

Full text: [Alliance Tax Justice and Cost of Living Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-tax-justice-cost-of-living-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-tax-justice-cost-of-living-policy-2026.pdf)); [Our Tax Plan Makes First $20,000 Income Tax-Free, Funded by Wealth Tax](documents/post-2026-09-06-alliance-tax-plan-first-20000-income-tax-free.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-tax-plan-first-20000-income-tax-free/)); [Alliance Tax Policy Costings 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-tax-policy-costings.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-tax-policy-costings-2026.pdf))

### Support small business with a public development bank, maximum payment terms and action against monopolies (ALL-20)

**How** (*archive*): Legislated maximum payment terms for large firms and agencies, automatic interest on overdue invoices, published payment times, stronger competition law, and support for co-operatives and new enterprises.

Full text: [Small Business, Local Enterprise, and Cooperative Development (PDF)](documents/pdf-small-business-local-enterprise-cooperative-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-small-business-local-enterprise-cooperative-policy-2026.pdf)); [Small Is Beautiful! Backing Small Business, Local Enterprise, and Cooperatives](documents/post-2026-09-17-alliance-small-business-local-enterprise-cooperati.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-small-business-local-enterprise-cooperatives/))

### Stop all further privatisation and return ports, water, telecommunications and Air New Zealand to full public ownership (ALL-26)

**How** (*archive*): Democratic accountability for public enterprises (including extending the OIA to Crown-controlled listed companies), worker board representation, and a Ministry of Development and public development bank.

Full text: [Alliance Public Ownership and Economic Democracy Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-public-ownership-economic-democracy-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/alliance-public-ownership-economic-democracy-policy-2026.pdf)); [Time to Take Back Our Power: Alliance Launches “Reverse Privatisation” Plan](documents/post-2026-10-02-alliance-public-ownership-economic-democracy-polic.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-public-ownership-economic-democracy-policy/))

## Education

### Pay a universal student income equivalent to the unemployment benefit (ALL-18)

**How** (*archive*): Independent of parental income, for tertiary and vocational students and trainees.

Full text: [Alliance Welfare Family and Social Security Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-welfare-family-social-security-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-welfare-family-social-security-policy-2026.pdf)); [Our Plan to Rebuild Universal Social Security](documents/post-2026-09-14-alliance-plan-to-rebuild-universal-social-security.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-plan-to-rebuild-universal-social-security/))

## Environment

### Replace the Emissions Trading Scheme with a carbon tax (ALL-10)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says a carbon tax sets a transparent price that free allocation and offsets cannot undermine.

**How** (*archive*): Revenue directed to renewables, public transport and emissions reduction; mandatory energy-efficiency standards for buildings, appliances, vehicles and industry.

Full text: [Alliance Environmental, Climate, and Sustainable Economy Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-environment-climate-sustainable-economy-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-environment-climate-sustainable-economy-policy-2026.pdf)); [Public Power, Clean Water, Polluters Pay: A Just Transition in Our Environment Policy](documents/post-2026-09-08-alliance-environment-climate-sustainable-economy-p.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-environment-climate-sustainable-economy-policy/))

### Apply a strict polluter-pays principle and move to a zero-waste, circular economy (ALL-11)

**How** (*archive*): Polluters pay full repair costs; ban non-recyclable plastic packaging, reusable packaging such as glass bottles, right to repair; keep water in public ownership with stronger pollution controls; a Genuine Progress Index alongside GDP.

Full text: [Alliance Environmental, Climate, and Sustainable Economy Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-environment-climate-sustainable-economy-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-environment-climate-sustainable-economy-policy-2026.pdf)); [Public Power, Clean Water, Polluters Pay: A Just Transition in Our Environment Policy](documents/post-2026-09-08-alliance-environment-climate-sustainable-economy-p.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-environment-climate-sustainable-economy-policy/))

### Ban mining in national parks, conservation land and the Coromandel, and give the Conservation Minister a veto (ALL-12)

**How** (*archive*): Restoration bonds for permitted mining, precaution on genetic modification, limits on sales of land and beaches to overseas buyers, and a reaffirmed nuclear-free policy.

Full text: [Alliance Environmental, Climate, and Sustainable Economy Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-environment-climate-sustainable-economy-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-environment-climate-sustainable-economy-policy-2026.pdf)); [Public Power, Clean Water, Polluters Pay: A Just Transition in Our Environment Policy](documents/post-2026-09-08-alliance-environment-climate-sustainable-economy-p.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-environment-climate-sustainable-economy-policy/))

## Health

### Create a public Community Health Service with free GP, dental, optical, audiology and mental-health care (ALL-13)

**Why** (*archive*): The Alliance says primary care is a fragmented network of struggling private practices.

**How** (*archive*): Fund care teams rather than appointments, bring allied services into public provision, give community health workers hospital-equivalent pay, uncap nurse-practitioner training, 'GP rescue' by taking over practice overheads, and local Community Health Boards.

Full text: [Alliance Health Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-health-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-health-policy-2026.pdf)); [Our Health Policy Eliminates Costs for GP Visits, Dental, Optical, and Audiology Services](documents/post-2026-09-10-alliance-health-policy-free-gp-dental-optical-audi.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-health-policy-free-gp-dental-optical-audiology/))

## Housing

### Clear the social housing waitlist in five years through a national state-house rebuilding programme (ALL-22)

**Why** (*archive*): The Alliance says housing is a fundamental human right.

**How** (*archive*): Funding Kāinga Ora for large-scale building with local materials and labour, cap Kāinga Ora rents and state-backed mortgage payments at 25% of net household income, no-deposit low-interest state loans for low-income workers, co-operative housing, stronger tenancy protections and universal insulation.

Full text: [Alliance Housing Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-housing-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-housing-policy-2026.pdf)); [The Right to a Roof: Our Housing Policy](documents/post-2026-09-23-the-right-to-a-roof-alliance-housing-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/the-right-to-a-roof-alliance-housing-policy/))

## Incomes & employment

### Make the first $20,000 of everyone's income tax-free (ALL-01)

**Why** (*archive*): The Alliance says income is taxed from the first dollar that pays for food, power and rent while wealth is lightly taxed.

**How** (*archive*): A universal, automatic threshold; it says everyone earning under about $178,150 would pay less. Upper rates of 34% ($78,100–$150,000), 39% ($150,000–$250,000) and 47% above $250,000.

Full text: [Alliance Tax Justice and Cost of Living Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-tax-justice-cost-of-living-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-tax-justice-cost-of-living-policy-2026.pdf)); [Our Tax Plan Makes First $20,000 Income Tax-Free, Funded by Wealth Tax](documents/post-2026-09-06-alliance-tax-plan-first-20000-income-tax-free.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-tax-plan-first-20000-income-tax-free/)); [Alliance Tax Policy Costings 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-tax-policy-costings.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-tax-policy-costings-2026.pdf))

### Introduce a 2.5% annual wealth tax on net wealth over $2 million, with a trust tax (ALL-02)

**How** (*archive*): A couple would pay nothing on combined net wealth up to $4 million; the party estimates $6.59 billion a year and would resource IRD to enforce it.

Full text: [Alliance Tax Justice and Cost of Living Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-tax-justice-cost-of-living-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-tax-justice-cost-of-living-policy-2026.pdf)); [Our Tax Plan Makes First $20,000 Income Tax-Free, Funded by Wealth Tax](documents/post-2026-09-06-alliance-tax-plan-first-20000-income-tax-free.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-tax-plan-first-20000-income-tax-free/)); [Alliance Tax Policy Costings 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-tax-policy-costings.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-tax-policy-costings-2026.pdf))

### Introduce a 33% capital gains tax on realised gains, excluding the family home (ALL-03)

**How** (*archive*): Covers investment property, shares and business assets, applying only to gains after it starts; revenue estimated to build from $0.54bn to over $2bn a year.

Full text: [Alliance Tax Justice and Cost of Living Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-tax-justice-cost-of-living-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-tax-justice-cost-of-living-policy-2026.pdf)); [Our Tax Plan Makes First $20,000 Income Tax-Free, Funded by Wealth Tax](documents/post-2026-09-06-alliance-tax-plan-first-20000-income-tax-free.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-tax-plan-first-20000-income-tax-free/)); [Alliance Tax Policy Costings 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-tax-policy-costings.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-tax-policy-costings-2026.pdf))

### Make full employment a central goal, with a 35-hour week and five weeks' annual leave (ALL-05)

**Why** (*archive*): The Alliance says work is a basic right.

**How** (*archive*): 35 hours without loss of pay, penal rates for overtime, a right to refuse unreasonable hours, and public job creation in infrastructure, housing, conservation and services.

Full text: [Alliance Workers’ Rights and Employment Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-workers-rights-employment-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-workers-rights-employment-policy-2026.pdf)); [Full Employment and a 35-Hour Week in Our Workers’ Rights Policy](documents/post-2026-09-07-alliance-full-employment-35-hour-week-workers-righ.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-full-employment-35-hour-week-workers-rights-policy/))

### Raise the adult minimum wage immediately to two-thirds of the average wage and index it to inflation (ALL-06)

**How** (*archive*): Apply the adult rate to workers of all ages and adjust annually for the cost of living.

Full text: [Alliance Workers’ Rights and Employment Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-workers-rights-employment-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-workers-rights-employment-policy-2026.pdf)); [Full Employment and a 35-Hour Week in Our Workers’ Rights Policy](documents/post-2026-09-07-alliance-full-employment-35-hour-week-workers-righ.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-full-employment-35-hour-week-workers-rights-policy/))

### Provide 52 weeks' paid parental leave for all workers and paid compassionate leave (ALL-07)

**How** (*archive*): Including part-time, casual and seasonal workers.

Full text: [Alliance Workers’ Rights and Employment Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-workers-rights-employment-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-workers-rights-employment-policy-2026.pdf)); [Full Employment and a 35-Hour Week in Our Workers’ Rights Policy](documents/post-2026-09-07-alliance-full-employment-35-hour-week-workers-righ.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-full-employment-35-hour-week-workers-rights-policy/)); [Women, Gender Equality, and Economic Security (PDF)](documents/pdf-women-gender-equality-economic-security-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-women-gender-equality-economic-security-policy-2026.pdf)); [52 Weeks’ Paid Parental Leave in Our Gender Equality Plan](documents/post-2026-09-16-alliance-52-weeks-paid-parental-leave-gender-equal.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-52-weeks-paid-parental-leave-gender-equality/))

### Restore national collective bargaining, a broad right to strike and Work Councils in firms with over 50 staff (ALL-08)

**How** (*archive*): Coordinated wage bargaining, protection for solidarity and some political strikes, worker voice on restructuring and technology, a Minimum Employment Code covering contractors and labour hire, tougher action on wage theft, and a national retraining and redeployment programme.

Full text: [Alliance Workers’ Rights and Employment Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-workers-rights-employment-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-workers-rights-employment-policy-2026.pdf)); [Full Employment and a 35-Hour Week in Our Workers’ Rights Policy](documents/post-2026-09-07-alliance-full-employment-35-hour-week-workers-righ.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-full-employment-35-hour-week-workers-rights-policy/))

### Introduce a Universal Benefit and abolish benefit sanctions, stand-downs and beneficiary debt (ALL-16)

**Why** (*archive*): The Alliance says welfare should provide security, not punishment.

**How** (*archive*): An adequate universal base payment, individualised entitlements regardless of relationship status, write-off of MSD debt, quarterly indexation to wages or CPI (whichever is higher), and payments to unpaid carers.

Full text: [Alliance Welfare Family and Social Security Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-welfare-family-social-security-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-welfare-family-social-security-policy-2026.pdf)); [Our Plan to Rebuild Universal Social Security](documents/post-2026-09-14-alliance-plan-to-rebuild-universal-social-security.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-plan-to-rebuild-universal-social-security/))

### Restore a Universal Child Benefit paid to every child's main carer, plus a Universal Early Years Benefit for under-threes (ALL-17)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says Working for Families and the In-Work Tax Credit leave out some of the families most in need.

**How** (*archive*): Non-means-tested, paid directly to the primary carer and indexed to average weekly earnings, as part of a plan to eliminate child poverty.

Full text: [Alliance Universal Child Benefit and Child Poverty Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-universal-child-benefit-and-child-poverty-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-universal-child-benefit-and-child-poverty-policy-2026.pdf)); [Alliance Party Plan to Eliminate Child Poverty](documents/post-2026-09-23-alliance-plan-to-eliminate-child-poverty.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-plan-to-eliminate-child-poverty/)); [Alliance Calls for Universal Child Benefit](documents/post-2026-08-19-alliance-calls-for-universal-child-benefit.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-calls-for-universal-child-benefit/)); [Alliance Welfare Family and Social Security Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-welfare-family-social-security-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-welfare-family-social-security-policy-2026.pdf)); [Our Plan to Rebuild Universal Social Security](documents/post-2026-09-14-alliance-plan-to-rebuild-universal-social-security.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-plan-to-rebuild-universal-social-security/))

### Keep NZ Super at 65, raise the married rate to 72.5% of the after-tax average wage, and end means-testing for long-term aged care (ALL-23)

**How** (*archive*): Also a Ministry for Senior Citizens, independent advocates for older people, subsidised transport and internet, and strengthening KiwiSaver.

Full text: [Alliance Retirement and Aged Care Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-retirement-and-aged-care-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-retirement-and-aged-care-policy-2026.pdf)); [Alliance Party Commits to 65 Retirement Age, Funding Aged Care Support, Supercharging KiwiSaver](documents/post-2026-09-25-alliance-retirement-aged-care-kiwisaver-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-retirement-aged-care-kiwisaver-policy/))

## Law, justice & government

### 'Three strikes and into treatment': rehabilitation-focused justice with no private prisons (ALL-21)

**Why** (*archive*): The Alliance says justice is about prevention, rehabilitation and support for victims, not just punishment.

**How** (*archive*): Community care orders and habilitation centres, restorative and marae-based justice, a victim compensation scheme, prisons kept public, expanded legal aid and public defenders, and recognition of tikanga.

Full text: [Alliance Justice Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-justice-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-justice-policy-2026.pdf)); [Justice Policy: “Three Strikes and into Treatment”](documents/post-2026-09-21-alliance-justice-policy-three-strikes-into-treatme.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-justice-policy-three-strikes-into-treatment/))

### Lower the MMP threshold to 3.5% and hold a public review toward a written constitution grounded in Te Tiriti (ALL-24)

**How** (*archive*): Strengthen the Waitangi Tribunal, consider Matike Mai recommendations, citizens' initiatives, a democratic decision on the monarchy, stronger select committees, OIA reform, conflict-of-interest rules and donation transparency and limits.

Full text: [Alliance Te Tiriti o Waitangi, Democracy, and Constitutional Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-te-tiriti-democracy-constitutional-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-te-tiriti-democracy-constitutional-policy-2026.pdf)); [Alliance Party: Redistribute Power, Honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi, Move Forward in Unity](documents/post-2026-09-26-alliance-te-tiriti-democracy-constitutional-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-te-tiriti-democracy-constitutional-policy/))

## Transport & infrastructure

### Put all electricity generation, transmission, distribution and retail into full public ownership (ALL-09)

**Why** (*archive*): The Alliance says public ownership allows long-term planning and affordable power.

**How** (*archive*): A 'reverse privatisation' programme buying back strategic assets at fair value, focused on renewables.

Full text: [Alliance Environmental, Climate, and Sustainable Economy Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-environment-climate-sustainable-economy-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-environment-climate-sustainable-economy-policy-2026.pdf)); [Public Power, Clean Water, Polluters Pay: A Just Transition in Our Environment Policy](documents/post-2026-09-08-alliance-environment-climate-sustainable-economy-p.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-environment-climate-sustainable-economy-policy/)); [Alliance Public Ownership and Economic Democracy Policy 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-public-ownership-economic-democracy-policy.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/alliance-public-ownership-economic-democracy-policy-2026.pdf)); [Time to Take Back Our Power: Alliance Launches “Reverse Privatisation” Plan](documents/post-2026-10-02-alliance-public-ownership-economic-democracy-polic.md) ([original](https://allianceparty.nz/alliance-public-ownership-economic-democracy-policy/))

### Build a 100% publicly owned integrated transport system with a State Shipping Line and 'KiwiPort' national port network (ALL-14)

**How** (*archive*): Rail and coastal shipping as freight backbones, full public ownership of Air New Zealand, close the coastal cargo (cabotage) exception, a national port hub-and-spoke model, and a National Transport Strategy replacing ad-hoc highway spending.

# Animal Justice Party Aotearoa New Zealand (AJP) — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **Animal Justice Party Aotearoa New Zealand (AJP)** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **38 policies** listed, backed by **51 full-text source documents**.

- Party website: <https://animaljustice.org.nz/>
- Registration: 16 August 2023 (Electoral Commission register)

## About this list

The Animal Justice Party publishes an Election 2026 Manifesto, a plain-language Policy Summary (ten campaign themes), a 2026 full policy platform PDF (~23,000 words), four policy packs, and 40+ individual policy pages, most with their own PDF. All were captured (web text via the WordPress API plus each linked PDF). The list below gives the ten summary themes (marked as headline policies) followed by each detailed policy page.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/animal-justice/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). Party claims (costs, statistics) are reported as the party's claims, not verified.

**Gaps and caveats.** Some individual policy PDFs date from 2024–2025 (publication dates are in each document's front matter); the party presents them as current. PDF text extraction splits decorative drop-capitals onto their own line.

## Headline policies

- [Ban the cruellest farming and fishing practices first (intensive winter grazing, fast-growing chicken breeds, live export, mutilations, bottom trawling), with a funded farmer transition](#ban-the-cruellest-farming-and-fishing-practices-first-intensive-winter-grazing-fast-growing-chicken-breeds-live-export-mutilations-bottom-trawling-with-a-funded-farmer-transition-ajp-01) — Economy
- [Recognise animals in law as sentient beings rather than property](#recognise-animals-in-law-as-sentient-beings-rather-than-property-ajp-02) — Community & inclusion
- [Make plant-based meals the default in schools, hospitals and public institutions, and remove GST from fruit, vegetables, legumes and nuts](#make-plant-based-meals-the-default-in-schools-hospitals-and-public-institutions-and-remove-gst-from-fruit-vegetables-legumes-and-nuts-ajp-03) — Health
- [Create an independent Commissioner for Animals with investigative and enforcement powers](#create-an-independent-commissioner-for-animals-with-investigative-and-enforcement-powers-ajp-04) — Community & inclusion
- [Make rehoming the default in council pounds, with euthanasia only as a last resort](#make-rehoming-the-default-in-council-pounds-with-euthanasia-only-as-a-last-resort-ajp-05) — Community & inclusion
- [End lethal and poison-based control of cats; use desexing, Trap-Neuter-Return and habitat restoration](#end-lethal-and-poison-based-control-of-cats-use-desexing-trap-neuter-return-and-habitat-restoration-ajp-06) — Environment
- [Remove GST from veterinary services and fund public and mobile vet clinics](#remove-gst-from-veterinary-services-and-fund-public-and-mobile-vet-clinics-ajp-07) — Community & inclusion

## Community & inclusion

### Recognise animals in law as sentient beings rather than property (AJP-02)

**Why** (*archive*): The AJP says the property classification makes meaningful protection very hard.

**How** (*archive*): Write sentience into legislation with enforceable protections and end codes of practice that let industries sidestep the Animal Welfare Act.

Full text: [Policy Summary](documents/policy-policy-summary.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/policies/policy-summary/)); [Election 2026 Manifesto](documents/election-2026-manifesto.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/election-2026/election-manifesto/)); [AJP 2026 Policy Platform — Election 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-ajp-2026-policy-platform-election-2026.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/AJP-2026-Policy-platform-election-2026.pdf)); [Legislative Foundations](documents/policy-legislative-foundations.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/policies/legislative-foundations/))

### Create an independent Commissioner for Animals with investigative and enforcement powers (AJP-04)

**Why** (*archive*): The AJP says welfare is overseen by MPI, the same ministry that promotes farm exports — a conflict of interest.

**How** (*archive*): Modelled on the Children's Commissioner, with funding for welfare research and accountability for enforcement agencies.

Full text: [Policy Summary](documents/policy-policy-summary.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/policies/policy-summary/)); [Election 2026 Manifesto](documents/election-2026-manifesto.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/election-2026/election-manifesto/)); [AJP 2026 Policy Platform — Election 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-ajp-2026-policy-platform-election-2026.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/AJP-2026-Policy-platform-election-2026.pdf)); [Commissioner for Animals](documents/policy-commissioner-for-animals.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/policies/commissioner-for-animals/)); [Commissioner for Animals](documents/policy-animal-rights-commissioner.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/policies/animal-rights-commissioner/)); [Regulatory Oversight and Enforcement](documents/policy-regulatory-oversight-and-enforcement.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/policies/regulatory-oversight-and-enforcement/))

### Make rehoming the default in council pounds, with euthanasia only as a last resort (AJP-05)

**Why** (*archive*): The AJP says 60% of dogs impounded in Auckland last year were killed rather than rehomed.

**How** (*archive*): Public reporting of pound outcomes by every council, fairer reclaim processes and fees, funded foster networks and wide access to desexing.

Full text: [Policy Summary](documents/policy-policy-summary.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/policies/policy-summary/)); [Election 2026 Manifesto](documents/election-2026-manifesto.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/election-2026/election-manifesto/)); [AJP 2026 Policy Platform — Election 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-ajp-2026-policy-platform-election-2026.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/AJP-2026-Policy-platform-election-2026.pdf))

### Remove GST from veterinary services and fund public and mobile vet clinics (AJP-07)

**Why** (*archive*): The AJP says vet bills force impossible choices on families.

**How** (*archive*): A national network of publicly funded and mobile clinics plus guaranteed funding for injured wildlife care and desexing.

Full text: [Policy Summary](documents/policy-policy-summary.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/policies/policy-summary/)); [Election 2026 Manifesto](documents/election-2026-manifesto.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/election-2026/election-manifesto/)); [AJP 2026 Policy Platform — Election 2026 (PDF)](documents/pdf-ajp-2026-policy-platform-election-2026.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/AJP-2026-Policy-platform-election-2026.pdf))

### Move animal-welfare oversight out of MPI into independent governance (AJP-19)

Full text: [Independent Animal Welfare Governance to Reduce Harm](documents/policy-independent-animal-welfare-governance-to-reduce-harm.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/policies/independent-animal-welfare-governance-to-reduce-harm/)); [Legislation and Regulation Reform for Animal Protection](documents/policy-legislation-and-regulation-reform-for-animal-protection.md) ([original](https://animaljustice.org.nz/policies/992453-2/))
