# Conservative Party NZ (Conservatives NZ) — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **Conservative Party NZ (Conservatives NZ)** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **19 policies** listed, backed by **27 full-text source documents**.

- Party website: <https://www.conservatives.nz/ (2026 campaign site: https://conservatives.org.nz/)>
- Registration: 6 October 2011 (Electoral Commission register)

## About this list

The Conservative Party NZ (called the New Conservatives in 2020–2023; leader Helen Houghton) has two websites: the party site conservatives.nz (policy summary, principles, and policy press releases from 2025–26) and a separate 2026 campaign site conservatives.org.nz, linked from the main site, with 14 policy pages (Overview, Health, Economy, Bureaucracy, Environment, Immigration, Policing, Climate, Agriculture, Child Protection, Tax Relief, Right to Life, Natural Resources, Energy). Both are captured; policies are listed below with the campaign page as the main source.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/conservative/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). Party claims (costs, statistics) are reported as the party's claims, not verified.

**Gaps and caveats.** Wix blog posts on conservatives.nz are rendered client-side; their text was recovered from the page's embedded data. The campaign Energy page's layout table extracted poorly (text is present but jumbled). Tax wording differs: the economy page says 'lower tax rate', a 2025 press release says 'flat tax rate'.

## Headline policies

- [Cut personal and company tax, align the company rate with the top personal rate, and lower GST to 12.5%](#cut-personal-and-company-tax-align-the-company-rate-with-the-top-personal-rate-and-lower-gst-to-125-con-01) — Incomes & employment
- [Stop taxing NZ Super (including for over-65s still working) and boarders' income in private homes](#stop-taxing-nz-super-including-for-over-65s-still-working-and-boarders-income-in-private-homes-con-02) — Incomes & employment
- [Tighten immigration toward skilled migrants and cap other net migration by the supply of housing, doctors and school places](#tighten-immigration-toward-skilled-migrants-and-cap-other-net-migration-by-the-supply-of-housing-doctors-and-school-places-con-05) — Migration
- [Leave the Paris Agreement, scrap the ETS and repeal all 'climate'-based taxes, laws and agencies](#leave-the-paris-agreement-scrap-the-ets-and-repeal-all-climate-based-taxes-laws-and-agencies-con-09) — Environment
- [Encourage oil and gas exploration with a Norway-style resource joint venture and sovereign investment fund](#encourage-oil-and-gas-exploration-with-a-norway-style-resource-joint-venture-and-sovereign-investment-fund-con-11) — Economy
- [Recognise an unborn child as a legal person from the third trimester](#recognise-an-unborn-child-as-a-legal-person-from-the-third-trimester-con-17) — Health

## Contents by topic

- [Community & inclusion](#community--inclusion) (1)
- [Defence & foreign affairs](#defence--foreign-affairs) (1)
- [Economy](#economy) (2)
- [Environment](#environment) (2)
- [Health](#health) (3)
- [Incomes & employment](#incomes--employment) (2)
- [Law, justice & government](#law-justice--government) (5)
- [Migration](#migration) (1)
- [Transport & infrastructure](#transport--infrastructure) (2)

## Community & inclusion

### Employment and services based on merit, 'one law for all', and 'a man is a man, and a woman is a woman' (CON-19)

**Why** (*archive*): The party opposes policies that divide people by race, ancestry, sex or identity.

**How** (*archive*): Listed among its 'policies that work' alongside limiting unskilled immigration and defending free speech and Judeo-Christian traditions.

Full text: [Our Policies](documents/site-policy.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/policy)); [Overview (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-overview.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/overview/))

## Defence & foreign affairs

### Review all trade agreements and pursue a neutral foreign policy with a support- and reconstruction-focused military (CON-18)

**How** (*archive*): Seek a balance between free trade and protectionism ('Trade before War'); avoid being drawn into conflicts that do not threaten NZ territory.

Full text: [Economic and Trade Policy](documents/news-new-policies-announcement.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/news/new-policies-announcement))

## Economy

### Oppose converting farmland to carbon forestry and oppose the Gene Technology Bill (CON-10)

**How** (*archive*): No incentives for permanent carbon forestry on productive land; keep restrictions on GMO field trials and release; revisit the Planning and Natural Environment Bills to make them workable and protect property rights.

Full text: [Agriculture (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-agriculture.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/agriculture/)); [Policy clarification on rural, environmental, and agricultural issues](documents/news-policy-clarification-on-rural-environmental-and-agricultural-issues.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/news/policy-clarification-on-rural%2C-environmental%2C-and-agricultural-issues))

### Encourage oil and gas exploration with a Norway-style resource joint venture and sovereign investment fund (CON-11)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says New Zealand has failed to secure a fair share of its resources.

**How** (*archive*): Public-private resource partnerships, royalties shared with local communities, environmental bonds, returns held in a New Zealand Investment Fund.

Full text: [Natural Resources (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-natural-resources.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/natural-resources/))

## Environment

### Leave the Paris Agreement, scrap the ETS and repeal all 'climate'-based taxes, laws and agencies (CON-09)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says there is no climate emergency and that climate policies raise food and energy costs and hurt the poor most.

**How** (*archive*): Remove fossil-fuel taxes and restrictions, abolish climate units in government, end energy subsidies of any kind, and stop public funding of methane research such as AgriZero.

Full text: [Climate (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-climate.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/climate/)); [Agriculture (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-agriculture.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/agriculture/))

### Create a Kermadec Ocean Sanctuary and overhaul fisheries management with cameras on all commercial vessels (CON-14)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says the sustainable fisheries regime is widely abused.

**How** (*archive*): Promote the Kermadec Ocean Sanctuary Bill and reinstall surveillance cameras on commercial vessels.

Full text: [Environment (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-environment.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/environment/)); [Has New Zealand Failed Its Oceans? Conservative Party Says Yes - Environment Policy update](documents/news-has-new-zealand-failed-its-oceans.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/news/has-new-zealand-failed-its-oceans))

## Health

### Make cutting hospital waiting times the top health priority, funded from bureaucracy, procurement and productivity savings (CON-04)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says the key issue is whether patients are treated in time, not how much is spent.

**How** (*archive*): Measure waits for elective surgery, specialists, diagnostics, cancer and ED; buy private capacity where it is quicker and competitive; grow the domestic workforce; link any extra funding to measurable results.

Full text: [Health (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-health.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/health/))

### Restrict irreversible gender-related medical procedures for minors and require parental involvement (CON-16)

**How** (*archive*): Independent assessment before significant intervention, evidence-based practice, parental involvement subject to safeguards, and independent review mechanisms.

Full text: [Child Protection (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-child-protection.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/child-protection/))

### Recognise an unborn child as a legal person from the third trimester (CON-17)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says every human life has inherent dignity.

**How** (*archive*): An Unborn Child (Legal Personhood and Rights) Act with a protected right to life, without criminalising pregnant women, plus a Pregnancy and Family Support Programme (support payment, housing security, support services, adoption options).

Full text: [Right to life (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-right-to-life.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/right-to-life/))

## Incomes & employment

### Cut personal and company tax, align the company rate with the top personal rate, and lower GST to 12.5% (CON-01)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says lower taxes improve compliance and investment and that New Zealand's rates should be no higher than Australia's.

**How** (*archive*): Also tackle public debt; a 2025 release calls for a 'flat tax rate' for individuals and companies.

Full text: [Economy (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-economy-1.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/economy-1/)); [Economic and Trade Policy](documents/news-new-policies-announcement.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/news/new-policies-announcement))

### Stop taxing NZ Super (including for over-65s still working) and boarders' income in private homes (CON-02)

**How** (*archive*): Remove NZ Super from taxable income, and exempt genuine home-sharing/boarder income with safeguards against commercial use.

Full text: [Tax Relief (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-superannuation.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/superannuation/))

## Law, justice & government

### Let mayors become full-time council CEOs and give ministers power to appoint and sack senior public servants (CON-03)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says unelected bureaucrats and advisers usurp the mandate of elected representatives.

**How** (*archive*): Elected representatives at local and national level would get wide powers to dismiss obstructive or incompetent staff; legislate to curtail 'unconstitutional bureaucratic power'.

Full text: [Bureaucracy (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-bureaucracy.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/bureaucracy/)); [Has New Zealand Lost Control of Its Own Government?](documents/news-has-new-zealand-lost-control-of-its-own-government.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/news/has-new-zealand-lost-control-of-its-own-government))

### Hold a Royal Commission of Inquiry into police under-performance and corruption (CON-06)

**Why** (*archive*): The party cites fabricated drink-drive tests and lost public trust.

**How** (*archive*): Also: refer prima facie criminal allegations against police and all deaths caused by police action to the courts; protect identities of police witnesses in international drug cases; review drone laws.

Full text: [Policing (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-policing.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/policing/)); [Announcement: Police Policy - Commission Of Inquiry Into Under Performance And Corruption](documents/news-police-policy-announcement.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/news/police-policy-announcement))

### Strengthen the IPCA: double its staff, quadruple its budget, and let it prosecute and name officers (CON-07)

**How** (*archive*): As set out in its 'Sharpening the Teeth of the IPCA' statement.

Full text: [Law & Justice Policy Statement: Sharpening the Teeth of the IPCA](documents/news-sharpening-the-teeth-of-the-ipca.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/news/sharpening-the-teeth-of-the-ipca))

### Improve access to justice for self-represented litigants (CON-08)

**How** (*archive*): Procedural changes, support services, legal aid reform, tax deductions and cost awards for pro bono work, and wider Family Dispute Resolution.

Full text: [Improving Access to Justice for Self-Represented Litigants](documents/news-press-release-improving-access-to-justice-for-self-represented-litigan.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/news/press-release---improving-access-to-justice-for-self-represented-litigants))

### Increase penalties for child sexual offending and online exploitation (CON-15)

**How** (*archive*): Longer sentences for serious and repeat offenders, review of sentence reductions, better monitoring after release, more online-exploitation investigation resources and victim support.

Full text: [Child Protection (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-child-protection.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/child-protection/))

## Migration

### Tighten immigration toward skilled migrants and cap other net migration by the supply of housing, doctors and school places (CON-05)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says population growing faster than 'social goods' makes everyone poorer.

**How** (*archive*): A stable points system; end 'golden' investor visas; NZ licence tests for foreign truck drivers; tougher document checks and audits; report GDP per capita.

Full text: [Immigration (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-immigration.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/immigration/))

## Transport & infrastructure

### Buy a fleet of oil tankers and build new oil refineries for fuel security (CON-12)

**How** (*archive*): Tankers would guarantee supply and floating storage until refineries able to process local and Pacific crude are built; also bring back manufacturing.

Full text: [Natural Resources (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-natural-resources.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/natural-resources/)); [Agriculture (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-agriculture.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/agriculture/))

### Ensure 'cheap, reliable and abundant' energy without relying solely on solar and wind (CON-13)

**How** (*archive*): Renewables have a role but cannot be relied on alone because of variability.

Full text: [Energy (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-energy.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/energy/))

# Free Palestine (Palestine Free from the River to the Sea Party) — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **Free Palestine (Palestine Free from the River to the Sea Party)** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **6 policies** listed, backed by **3 full-text source documents**.

- Party website: <https://palfree.nz/>
- Registration: 5 August 2026 as "Free Palestine" (Electoral Commission register)

## About this list

Free Palestine is a single-issue party registered in August 2026 (its website calls it the 'Palestine Free from the River to the Sea Party'). Its platform consists of three objectives and six founding principles on its one-page website, the same principles in its June 2026 constitution lodged with the Electoral Commission, and a six-point list in its August 2026 registration press release. Each principle/objective is listed below.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/free-palestine/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). Party claims (costs, statistics) are reported as the party's claims, not verified.

**Gaps and caveats.** The party has no published policies on domestic issues. Wording differs slightly between sources: the website refers to dismantling 'the Zionist structure of the state of Israel', the constitution to 'the apartheid structure'. Media reports of a separate 2026 foreign-affairs policy could not be checked against a party document (web search capacity ran out). The website's membership, enrolment and donation sections are omitted from the captured text.

## Headline policies

- [Support the right of return of Palestinian refugees and the dismantling of Israel's current state structure, rejecting a two-state solution](#support-the-right-of-return-of-palestinian-refugees-and-the-dismantling-of-israels-current-state-structure-rejecting-a-two-state-solution-fpp-01) — Defence & foreign affairs
- [Establish a single secular, democratic, bi-national state in all of historic Palestine with equal citizenship](#establish-a-single-secular-democratic-bi-national-state-in-all-of-historic-palestine-with-equal-citizenship-fpp-02) — Defence & foreign affairs
- [Adopt an independent foreign policy and withdraw from formal military and security alliances with the United States](#adopt-an-independent-foreign-policy-and-withdraw-from-formal-military-and-security-alliances-with-the-united-states-fpp-05) — Defence & foreign affairs

## Contents by topic

- [Defence & foreign affairs](#defence--foreign-affairs) (6)

## Defence & foreign affairs

### Support the right of return of Palestinian refugees and the dismantling of Israel's current state structure, rejecting a two-state solution (FPP-01)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says a just peace depends on refugees' return and that further partition would bring more injustice.

**How** (*archive*): Founding principle 1 (website) / constitution clause 2.

Full text: [Palestine Free from the River to the Sea Party — Objectives and Founding Principles](documents/palfree-home-objectives-principles.md) ([original](https://palfree.nz/)); [Free Palestine Party Constitution (June 2026, as lodged with the Electoral Commission)](documents/constitution-june-2026.md) ([original](https://elections.nz/assets/Party-rules/FPP-Constitution-June-2026.pdf)); [The Free Palestine Party: The Newest Political Party In Aotearoa](documents/release-2026-08-newest-political-party.md) ([original](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2608/S00073/the-free-palestine-party-the-newest-political-party-in-aotearoa.htm))

# Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand — every 2026 election policy

*Compiled 2026-10-23 for the 7 November 2026 general election. Part of a non-partisan archive; every item links to its source and, wherever it could be retrieved, to the full verbatim text in [`documents/`](documents/).*

## Changes on policy.nz since 23 October 2026

This archive captured the party's policy.nz policies on 23 October 2026; policy.nz is re-checked daily by [`tools/refresh_policies.py`](../../../tools/refresh_policies.py). Nothing is deleted: a policy that is no longer on policy.nz stays in this archive marked *withdrawn*. Full texts of new sources are archived separately; until then the links go to the original pages. Where this block and the sections below differ, this block is the newer text.

### New policies

#### Pay students who need to complete work placements for their qualifications (POL55328)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that students completing important jobs, like midwifery, nursing, social work and teaching, are required to complete paid work hours to receive their qualifications. These students must show up for as much as 30 hours a week, making it difficult to hold down another job. This party says that as NZ needs more of the people completing these qualifications, people on work placements should be paid, and supported if they are completing placements in other parts of the country.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would support students completing work placements for their study with a payment of $380 a week, on top of existing student loans or student allowances. Students who had to relocate for a placement (for example to a different region) would receive a one-off relocation payment of $1500.

Sources: ['Greens announce paid placements for nurses, teachers, and social workers', 16 October 2026 (accessed 21 October 2026)](https://www.greens.org.nz/greens_announce_paid_placements_for_nurses_teachers_and_social_workers); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/green-party). Full text not yet archived.

#### Provide $2000 to employers and apprentices to help with training (POL55329)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that for NZ's economy to get stronger, it needs a strong workforce. However, apprentice numbers are at a 15-year low. This party says that investing in people is a way to grow the workforce and economy and help apprentices to be supported in their chosen fields of work. Employers should also receive a financial incentive for supporting apprentices to complete their training.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would give apprentices a $2000 equipment grant for buying tools, equipment or uniforms required for their qualification. Employers who take on apprentices who finish their qualifications would receive $2000 when the apprentice finishes training.

Sources: ['Green Party to abolish training wage and provide more support for apprentices ', undated (accessed 21 October 2026)](https://www.greens.org.nz/green_party_to_abolish_training_wage_and_provide_more_support_for_apprentices); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/green-party). Full text not yet archived.

#### Abolish the training wage (POL55330)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that apprentice numbers are at a 15 year low, even though the ork apprentices do is important and needed. Low pay and insecure work prevent people from entering the trades, this party says. It wants to abolish the training wage, which allows apprentices or people in training to be paid less than the minimum wage for work they complete.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would abolish the training wage. All workers, regardless of training status, would be paid the minimum wage.

Sources: ['Green Party to abolish training wage and provide more support for apprentices ', undated (accessed 21 October 2026)](https://www.greens.org.nz/green_party_to_abolish_training_wage_and_provide_more_support_for_apprentices); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/green-party). Full text not yet archived.

#### Invest $30m in Māori and Pacific led trades training (POL55331)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that NZ needs more homes and renewable energy, and needs people who can do this work, such as builders nad electricians. However, apprentice numbers are at a 15-year low. It says that Māori and Pacific people face extra financial and structural barriers to completing training and this group should be supported specifically.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would create a $30m funding lift each year for Māori and Pasifika-led trades training. This will include pastoral care, job matches and wraparound services for newly qualified workers.

Sources: ['Green Party to abolish training wage and provide more support for apprentices ', undated (accessed 21 October 2026)](https://www.greens.org.nz/green_party_to_abolish_training_wage_and_provide_more_support_for_apprentices); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/green-party). Full text not yet archived.

#### Change the Investment Boost funding to focus on decarbonisation (POL55334)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that the NZ economy is important and must respond to the needs of New Zealanders, like good jobs and reducing emissions. It says the current Investment Boost scheme should be refocused on productive investments that create jobs with appropriate working conditions and low-emissions industries. As part of an overall jobs package, this party says this would create 284,000 jobs.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would refocus the "Investment Boost" government funding for businesses on businesses aligned with investment objectives, decarbonisation and good quality working conditions.

Sources: ['Greens’ economic development plan will create 284,000 jobs ', undated (accessed 19 October 2026)](https://www.greens.org.nz/greens_economic_development_plan_will_create_284_000_jobs); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/green-party). Full text not yet archived.

#### Establish industry partnerships for mid-and-early career researchers (POL55335)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that the NZ economy is currently growing at 1.5 percent, not the 2 percent needed for an international benchmark for a competitive economy. NZ should invest in future researchers in specific industry areas to increase productivity in the future.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would create "mission fellowships" for early and mid career researchers and technical specialists, completing research linked to specific objectives of their industries.

Sources: ['Greens’ economic development plan will create 284,000 jobs ', undated (accessed 19 October 2026)](https://www.greens.org.nz/greens_economic_development_plan_will_create_284_000_jobs); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/green-party). Full text not yet archived.

#### Increase funding for research and science in NZ (POL55336)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that NZ's economy needs to grow, and science and technology research can create big new ideas. It says the current government has decreased science funding and this investment needs to increase again.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would restore science funding lost through cuts, with the goal of spending 3 percent of GDP on research and development. It would also increase funding for research in tertiary education centres, including initiatives like the centres of vocational excellence.

Sources: ['Greens’ economic development plan will create 284,000 jobs ', undated (accessed 19 October 2026)](https://www.greens.org.nz/greens_economic_development_plan_will_create_284_000_jobs); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/green-party). _Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that NZ's GDP should move towards growing 2 percent or 3 percent a year, rather than the current 1.5 percent. Increasing economic growth for innovative ideas can create jobs, especially if businesses with good ideas are supported to scale their products.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would create a co-ordinated pathway for NZ businesses to grow exports, moving from research and experiments to commercial-scale production. To support businesses, it would also make sure public procurement contracts are given to NZ companies.

Sources: ['Greens’ economic development plan will create 284,000 jobs ', undated (accessed 19 October 2026)](https://www.greens.org.nz/greens_economic_development_plan_will_create_284_000_jobs); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/green-party). Full text not yet archived.

#### Protect at least 30 percent of the Hauraki Gulf by 2030 (POL55338)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that it wants to protect at least 30 percent of NZ's oceans by 2030, including the Hauraki Gulf. It says this area around Auckland should be restored so biodiversity can flourish and people can swim and fish in the area.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would commit to the goal of protecting at least 30 percent of the Hauraki Gulf by 2030. It would remove the ring-net fishing exemption from the Hauraki Gulf. This party says some of its other policies would also help the Gulf, including reducing bycatch with cameras on fisheries boats; resourcing iwi to lead ocean protection efforts; phase out synthetic nitrogen fertiliser and wastewater discharge limits to improve water quality and phasing out bottom trawling in significant areas and seamounts.

Sources: ['Greens announce plan to protect the Hauraki Gulf ', 6 October 2026 (accessed 15 October 2026)](https://www.greens.org.nz/greens_announce_plans_to_protect_the_hauraki_gulf); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/green-party). Full text not yet archived.

#### Increase public health funding by $3bn over 4 years (POL55370)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that NZ's health system needs long term planning and funding to create good outcomes. To rebuild lost capacity, this party says further investment is needed. Under its fiscal plan, it would create long-term workforce plans and fund the health system further.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would increase public health funding by $3bn over four years, so the total would be $30bn spent on health by the end of that period. This money would go to long-term planning as well as immediate needs.

Sources: ['Greens to deliver more staff, shorter wait times and a healthier country with significant health investment', 23 October 2026 (accessed 27 October 2026)](https://www.greens.org.nz/greens_to_deliver_more_staff_shorter_wait_times_and_a_healthier_country_with_significant_health_investment); ['Green's Fiscal Plan builds real economic resilience to lower cost of living and stimulate 64000 new jobs', 23 October 2026 (accessed 27 October 2026)](https://www.greens.org.nz/greens_fiscal_plan_builds_real_economic_resilience_to_lower_cost_of_living_and_stimulate_64_000_new_jobs); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/green-party). Full text not yet archived.

#### Aim to create a government surplus by 2029/30 (POL55371)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that public investment is essential for economic development, productivity and resilience. This party says government investment can help grow NZ's economy and multiply impact later on. It says the government should increase revenue by creating a wealth tax, focusing on taxing capital and assets rather than productive work. Along with economic growth, this party says this plan will return the government to surplus while also creating better outcomes for New Zealanders.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would return the government to surplus by 2029/30. It would do this by increasing the tax base, prioritising taxing capital (i.e. a wealth tax) rather than labour.

#### Commit to future government operating allowances between $4.5bn to $4.7 bn (POL55372)

## About this page

- **226 policy statements from [policy.nz](https://policy.nz)** (the independent, non-partisan guide), each with its *Why* and *How* summary exactly as policy.nz wrote it, its topics and its citations. These are the core of this page.
- **245 verbatim "Our plan" commitments** from the 38 chapters of the Green Party Manifesto 2026 (launched 26 July 2026), so that every manifesto commitment is listed even where policy.nz did not write it up. These are quoted exactly; they have no separate summary.
- **93 further entries** for party policy documents and 2026 campaign announcements, with a short neutral summary written for this archive (marked `summary_source: "archive"` in [`policies.json`](policies.json)).
- **185 full-text documents** in [`documents/`](documents/): 54 PDFs (manifesto, Māori manifesto, Easy Read manifesto, 40 standing policy papers, 2026 campaign policy papers, Green Budget 2025), 123 greens.org.nz pages and 8 press releases mirrored on Scoop.

**How the text was obtained.** greens.org.nz is behind Cloudflare and refuses automated access (HTTP 403), and the Internet Archive (web.archive.org) could not be reached from the research environment. So:
1. **PDFs** were downloaded directly from the party's file host `assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/…` (and two from `img.scoop.co.nz`) and converted with `pdftotext`. Reading order was checked; the default (non-layout) mode was cleaner for the multi-column brochures, and pages that contain tables are additionally reproduced in `-layout` form so that table rows stay intact. One image-only PDF (the KiwiPower explainer) was transcribed by hand and is marked as such. Local copies are in `raw/party-docs/green/pdf/`.
2. **greens.org.nz web pages** (manifesto chapters, policy summary pages, press releases) were recovered from **Common Crawl** WARC captures (crawls CC-MAIN-2026-30, -34, -39 and -43, i.e. July to 18 October 2026); each document records its capture date.
3. **Press releases not captured by Common Crawl** were taken from the copies the party posted on **scoop.co.nz**.
4. Nothing was paraphrased inside a full-text document. Where a source could not be retrieved the document says so.

## Headline commitments

policy.nz marks these as the Greens' **key policies**:

- **Create a 2.5 percent tax on assets worth over $10m** (Economy). [POL54655](#pol54655)
- **Implement a tax on wealth received over $1m** (Economy). [POL54729](#pol54729)
- **Increase the corporate tax rate to 33 percent for big corporations only** (Economy). [POL54730](#pol54730)
- **Make the first $10,000 that people earn tax-free** (Incomes and employment). [POL54735](#pol54735)
- **Create a new tax bracket for income earned over $160,000** (Incomes and employment). [POL54737](#pol54737)
- **Establish a government backed clean energy loan scheme** (Environment). [POL54744](#pol54744)
- **Mandate the installation of solar on new or renovated public homes, where appropriate** (Housing). [POL54764](#pol54764)
- **Create a job guarantee programme for jobs focused on ecosystem regeneration** (Incomes and employment). [POL54787](#pol54787)
- **Provide stable funding for creative organisations and events** (Media, culture and recreation). [POL54954](#pol54954)
- **Support the repatriation of taonga overseas back to the Māori community** (Media, culture and recreation). [POL54956](#pol54956)
- **Establish infrastructure across ministries to strengthen our creative and cultural economy** (Media, culture and recreation). [POL54957](#pol54957)
- **Provide $200m towards te reo Māori initiatives** (Te ao Māori). [POL54979](#pol54979)
- **Expand voting rights in New Zealand** (Law, justice and government). [POL54981](#pol54981)
- **Entrench the Māori electoral seats** (Law, justice and government). [POL54982](#pol54982)
- **Strengthen political lobbying rules** (Law, justice and government). [POL54984](#pol54984)
- **Remove barriers to accessing essential services for disabled people** (Health). [POL55004](#pol55004)
- **Ensure rainbow communities can access gender-affirming healthcare** (Health). [POL55010](#pol55010)
- **Restore the monitoring role of the Children's Commissioner** (Community and inclusion). [POL55019](#pol55019)
- **Allow people with Māori whakapapa to become New Zealand citizens no matter where they are born** (Te ao Māori). [POL55024](#pol55024)
- **Make it easier for people based in other countries to repay student loans** (Education). [POL55027](#pol55027)
- **Pursue reciprocal healthcare, welfare and visa-waiver arrangements with other countries** (Migration). [POL55028](#pol55028)
- **Introduce free public transport fares for young people, the disabled and CSC card holders** (Transport and infrastructure). [POL55029](#pol55029)
- **Build mass rapid transit in three major cities and invest in better rail and bus links** (Transport and infrastructure). [POL55030](#pol55030)
- **Break up the supermarket duopoly and use part of it to create a government-owned supermarket** (Economy). [POL55032](#pol55032)
- **Increase climate aid funding to the Pacific** (Defence and foreign affairs). [POL55034](#pol55034)
- **Introduce fees-free tertiary education, universal student allowances and paid placements** (Education). [POL55035](#pol55035)
- **Increase visa-free travel and work visa set-ups for Pasifika visitors and workers in NZ** (Defence and foreign affairs). [POL55036](#pol55036)

The party's campaign is built around three priorities: "affordable living, healthy nature and real democracy". It is to be paid for by taxing "the super-rich and mega-corporations" while cutting income tax "for 96 percent of people" ([manifesto introduction](documents/web-manifesto-2026.md)). The main policy packages released during 2026 were:

- **Tax policy 'A tax system for all of us': wealth tax, capital acquisitions tax, higher tax on big corporates, bank levy, and income tax cuts for 96% of earners**: The 12-page tax plan (announced 21 June 2026). Revenue measures: a 2.5% tax on the net assets of the super-rich above $10 million (family homes exempt); a capital acquisitions tax on gifts and inheritances over $1 million (family farms and homes exempt); a 33% company tax rate for the largest 0.7% of companies while small and medium firms stay at 28%; a 0.06% levy on the liabilities of the four big banks; enforcing a 5% withholding tax on big tech profits sent offshore; and reversing the coalition's landlord interest-deductibility and bright-line changes. Income tax: a $10,000 tax-free threshold, new stepped brackets and a 45% rate above $160,000. The party's own Parliamentary-Library-based modelling puts the net gain at about $5.1-5.7 billion a year (2027/28-2030/31). [full text](documents/tax-policy-2026-a-tax-system-for-all-of-us.md)
- **'Drink Swim Fish' freshwater and oceans policy**: A 4-page water policy (announced 6 July 2026) aimed at safe drinking water, swimmable rivers and healthier oceans: science-based national freshwater limits including lower nitrate limits, stronger wastewater-discharge rules, phasing out synthetic nitrogen fertiliser, phasing out bottom trawling and other destructive fishing, protecting at least 30% of oceans, and reviewing the fisheries quota system. [full text](documents/drink-swim-fish-policy-2026.md)
- **'Power for all of us' energy policy: Kiwipower, Warmer Kiwi Homes expansion, community energy and zero-interest solar loans**: The 12-page energy policy (announced 20 July 2026). It proposes 'Kiwipower', a publicly owned company to contract and build electricity firming; an expanded Warmer Kiwi Homes insulation/heating programme; $200m for community-owned energy; a government-backed Clean Energy Loans Scheme (modelled as zero-interest, tied to the property) for rooftop solar and other home energy upgrades; and other electricity-market changes. It includes four-year cost tables and says spending would be funded by the proposed super-rich tax. [full text](documents/power-for-all-of-us-policy-2026.md)
- **Te Waonui a Tāne: an ongoing, protected funding source for marae**: An 11-page policy (announced 9 August 2026) to recognise and resource marae as social and cultural infrastructure. It proposes a Rangatiratanga Trust with a $2.44 billion Crown funding input, including a $2 billion intergenerational fund (Te Tōtara Haemata) and annual restoration funding for marae, governed with regional marae representation. [full text](documents/te-waonui-a-tane-policy-2026.md)
- **'Affordable food for all of us': KiwiMart public supermarket chain, stronger grocery regulation and a Fair Food Fund**: A 15-page food-system policy (announced 6 September 2026). It proposes a publicly owned supermarket chain 'KiwiMart' (estimated acquisition and capitalisation cost about $2.8bn, citing an estimate of $1.3bn to buy 120 stores and two distribution centres), more Commerce Commission funding and higher penalties for grocery-sector breaches, a $150m Fair Food Fund for community food security, and more funding for regional food providers. [full text](documents/affordable-food-for-all-of-us-policy-2026.md)
- **'Safe, sovereign AI': regulate artificial intelligence for the public good**: An 8-page AI plan (announced 12 October 2026). It proposes rules so that AI does not replace human or democratic decision-making (no fully automated decisions with substantive effects in public services), protects data sovereignty, privacy and creators' work, operates within environmental limits (including controls on data centres), shares benefits rather than concentrating them, and is transparent and accountable. [full text](documents/ai-policy-2026-safe-sovereign-ai.md)
- **Youth Jobs Guarantee: a job or training pathway for every 16-24-year-old out of work for six months**: A 7-page jobs policy (published October 2026) guaranteeing every 16-to-24-year-old who has been out of work for six months a pathway into a locally based job or training, delivered with councils and building on the Mayors Taskforce for Jobs. The document's indicative costings rise from $604m in the first year to $1,631m in the fourth. [full text](documents/youth-jobs-guarantee-policy-2026.md)
- **Paid placements for trainee nurses, teachers and social workers; abolish the training wage for apprentices**: A 4-page workforce policy (16-17 October 2026): a universal weekly payment for students during compulsory practical placements (nursing, teaching, social work and similar), relocation support, abolition of the training-wage exemption so apprentices get at least the minimum wage, a grant for apprentices' tools, and more pastoral support. Indicative costs are about $75-80m and $117m a year for the two parts. [full text](documents/paid-placements-apprenticeships-policy-2026.md)
- **Connect: Aotearoa transport plan**: 4 Oct 2026: transport plan with free public transport for children, students, Community Service Card holders and Total Mobility users, a $2 fare cap for everyone else, bus lanes in the three main cities and mass rapid transit. [full text](documents/web-green-party-launches-the-transport-plan-to-combat-fossil-fuel-crisis.md), [policy page](documents/web-connect-aotearoa.md)

**Tax plan revenue.** The table below gives the party's own estimates from *A tax system for all of us* (page 10). Figures are $ million per year; negative figures are revenue forgone. The document says the estimates come from Parliamentary Library models, with an allowance for avoidance and evasion of the super-rich tax.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| Capital Acquisitions Tax | 953 | 1,001 | 1,051 | 1,103 |

| Major banks levy | 373 | 388 | 404 | 420 |
| Big tech tax | 204 | 214 | 223 | 233 |
| Reversing bright-line test changes | 45 | 45 | 45 | 45 |
| Reversing landlord tax cuts | 876 | 922 | 970 | 1,003 |
| Tax setting changes (income tax cuts) | -2,335 | -2,439 | -2,557 | -2,680 |

Source: [tax policy, full text](documents/tax-policy-2026-a-tax-system-for-all-of-us.md) (the table is reproduced in layout form on page 10).

**Fiscal plan (23 October 2026).** The party released its overall fiscal plan at Parliament on 23 October 2026. The document itself could not be retrieved here. According to [RNZ's report](https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics_election-2026/2097318/green-party-releases-fiscal-plan-promises-to-increase-health-spending-by-3-billion-each-year) (Russell Palmer, 23 Oct 2026), the plan:
- adds $3 billion to health funding in each of the next four Budgets, about $30 billion over the period;
- relies on "nearly $29 billion in extra revenue over four years" from the wealth tax, the tax on large gifts and inheritances, higher company tax for big businesses, a bank levy and landlord tax changes, alongside income tax cuts for most workers;
- raises future operating allowances to $4.5b–$4.7b a year, compared with about $2.4b under the coalition's plans;
- returns to surplus in 2029/30, a year later than Treasury forecasts, and leaves debt $26.6 billion higher than Treasury expects by 2030/31;
- commits future Budget funding to buying overseas carbon credits. Treasury estimated that bill could reach $5 billion; the Greens say more domestic cuts would reduce it.
Infometrics reviewed the plan's direct fiscal effects. Swarbrick said every election policy had been costed, and that the party still wants a Parliamentary Budget Office. National (Simeon Brown) and ACT (David Seymour) criticised the plan; their reactions are in the same RNZ report. Other outlets' coverage gave a debt figure of 44% of GDP by 2030/31 against Treasury's 39.5%. That figure has not been verified against the party document.

**Costings in individual policy papers.** Most 2026 policy papers end with four-year cost tables (2027/28–2030/31). These include [Power for all of us](documents/power-for-all-of-us-policy-2026.md), [KiwiPower](documents/kiwipower-explainer-2026.md), [Te Waonui a Tāne](documents/te-waonui-a-tane-policy-2026.md), [Affordable food](documents/affordable-food-for-all-of-us-policy-2026.md), [Youth Jobs Guarantee](documents/youth-jobs-guarantee-policy-2026.md) and [Paid placements & apprenticeships](documents/paid-placements-apprenticeships-policy-2026.md). Release-level costings include pay equity for care workers (about $1.1bn a year), cancelling public-service cuts ($3.17bn over four years) and te reo Māori ($200m). The party's 2025 alternative budget, [Green Budget 2025](documents/green-budget-2025.md), includes a full fiscal summary.

## Economy

### Policies (policy.nz)

<a id="pol54655"></a>
**Create a 2.5 percent tax on assets worth over $10m** ⭐ key policy  
`POL54655` · topics: incomes-and-employment, economy, tax-and-income-support, key-policies-economy, government-revenue-and-finance

- **Why:** This party says that the richest 311 households in NZ pay an effective tax rate of 9 percent, half that of most working people. This is because much of this wealth sits in asset portfolios, rather than being taxed as income. The wealthy need to contribute to solving shared problems with the rest of New Zealand. With the 150 richest people in NZ holding as much as 917,000 households, it is important to ensure the wealthy contribute through taxes.
- **How:** This party would implement a 2.5 percent annual tax on the net assets of people holding over $10m in wealth. This would affect 0.3 percent of New Zealanders.
- **Full text:** ['A tax system for all of us' (PDF), undated](documents/tax-policy-2026-a-tax-system-for-all-of-us.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/71965/attachments/original/1782084525/GreensTaxPolicy2026.pdf?1782084525)); ['Income', undated (accessed 13 August 2026)](documents/web-manifesto-2026-income.md) ([original](https://www.greens.org.nz/manifesto_2026_income))

<a id="pol54729"></a>
**Implement a tax on wealth received over $1m** ⭐ key policy  
`POL54729` · topics: incomes-and-employment, economy, tax-and-income-support, key-policies-economy, government-revenue-and-finance

- **Why:** This party says that more than $1.6 trillion in wealth is passed on intergenerationally. The party believes that being rich shouldn't be determined by who your parents are.
- **How:** This party would introduce a Capital Acquisitions Tax on assets and gifts received worth more than $1m. Family farms and family homes would be exempt.
- **Full text:** ['A tax system for all of us' (PDF), undated](documents/tax-policy-2026-a-tax-system-for-all-of-us.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/71965/attachments/original/1782084525/GreensTaxPolicy2026.pdf?1782084525)); ['Policy Announcement - A tax system for all of us', undated (accessed 24 August 2026)](documents/web-tax-system-for-all.md) ([original](https://www.greens.org.nz/tax_system_for_all))

<a id="pol54730"></a>
**Increase the corporate tax rate to 33 percent for big corporations only** ⭐ key policy  
`POL54730` · topics: economy, incomes-and-employment, business-support, government-revenue-and-finance, key-policies-economy, tax-and-income-support

- **Why:** This party says that large corporations in NZ are profiting from the public without contributing back towards society. It says that cuts to the corporate tax rate have not increased wellbeing, growth or investment for most New Zealanders; rather, corporations see more profits.
- **How:** This party would return the corporate tax rate to 33 percent for the 0.7 percent biggest corporations, such as the supermarket duopoly, energy companies, and banks. It would keep the corporate tax rate at  28 percent for small and medium enterprises. It would also introduce a Bank Levy of 0.06 percent on the liabilities of the four main banks. It would also enforce the 5 percent tax rate on service and license fees for large tech companies.
- **Full text:** ['A tax system for all of us' (PDF), undated](documents/tax-policy-2026-a-tax-system-for-all-of-us.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/71965/attachments/original/1782084525/GreensTaxPolicy2026.pdf?1782084525)); ['Policy Announcement - A tax system for all of us', undated (accessed 24 August 2026)](documents/web-tax-system-for-all.md) ([original](https://www.greens.org.nz/tax_system_for_all))

<a id="pol54742"></a>
**Phase out certain fishing practices**  
`POL54742` · topics: economy, environment, fisheries, oceans, conservation

- **Why:** This party says that bottom trawling, set netting, dredging and seamounts are destructive fishing practices, destroying native ecosystems and catching endangered species such as the Māui and Hector's dolphins. Banning these fishing practices would protect NZ's ocean ecosystems for generations to come.
- **How:** This party would phase out bottom trawling, set netting and dredging, starting with an immediate ban on seamounts. The focus on banning these fishing practices would begin in ecologically sensitive areas such as Tīkapa Moana/Hauraki Gulf and the habitats of Māui and Hector's dolphins.
- **Full text:** ['Oceans and Fisheries', undated (accessed 13 August 2026)](documents/web-manifesto-2026-oceans-and-fisheries.md) ([original](https://www.greens.org.nz/manifesto_2026_oceans_and_fisheries)); ['Drink Swim Fish Fixing the rules for fresh water and oceans' (PDF), undated (accessed 24 August 2026)](documents/drink-swim-fish-policy-2026.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/74309/attachments/original/1783476578/DSF_Policy_2026.pdf?1783476578)); ['Policy Announcement - Drink, Swim, Fish — Fixing the rules for water', undated (accessed 24 August 2026)](documents/web-drink-swim-fish.md) ([original](https://www.greens.org.nz/drink_swim_fish))

<a id="pol54743"></a>
**Review the quota system for fisheries**  
`POL54743` · topics: economy, environment, fisheries, oceans

- **Why:** This party says that the current fisheries rules allow for overfishing, depleting NZ's oceans. It wants to replenish our fish stocks with an improved management system which is founded on ecosystem protection.
- **How:** This party would review the Quota Management System and move towards ecosystem-based fisheries management that prioritises abundance and long-term sustainability.
- **Full text:** ['Oceans and Fisheries', undated (accessed 13 August 2026)](documents/web-manifesto-2026-oceans-and-fisheries.md) ([original](https://www.greens.org.nz/manifesto_2026_oceans_and_fisheries)); ['Drink Swim Fish Fixing the rules for fresh water and oceans' (PDF), undated (accessed 24 August 2026)](documents/drink-swim-fish-policy-2026.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/74309/attachments/original/1783476578/DSF_Policy_2026.pdf?1783476578)); ['Policy Announcement - Drink, Swim, Fish — Fixing the rules for water', undated (accessed 24 August 2026)](documents/web-drink-swim-fish.md) ([original](https://www.greens.org.nz/drink_swim_fish))

<a id="pol54904"></a>
**Establish an Agricultural Standards Framework**  
`POL54904` · topics: economy, agriculture

- **Why:** This party says that New Zealand needs strong agricultural standards to ensure it remains known for its premium-quality and environmentally sustainable products.
- **How:** This party would establish an Agricultural Standards Framework that includes requirements to measure all agricultural inputs and outputs, and robust and consistent measures of environmental impacts caused by agriculture. <a id="pol54905"></a>
**Prohibit palm kernel expeller (PKE) imports**  
`POL54905` · topics: economy, agriculture

### Manifesto 2026 commitments (verbatim)

**Digital Technology**: *Technology helping, not harming.* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2026-digital-technology.md))

1. Regulate social media platforms to address harmful content and behaviour by introducing a Digital Duty of Care. This will require algorithmic transparency and accessible and responsive complaints systems, as well as strengthening enforcement with an independent national regulator.
2. Regulate artificial intelligence to ensure its use is safe, transparent and accurate,
3. Crack down on tax avoidance and the offshoring of profits by multinational tech giants such as Meta, Amazon and Microsoft.
4. Adopt and implement the Māori Data Governance Model and Māori AI Governance Framework from Te Kāhui Raraunga across the public sector to protect Māori data sovereignty.
5. Strengthen obligations on data-holders to protect user and biometric data, increase penalties for privacy breaches, and strengthen enforcement powers for the Privacy Commissioner to better protect personal information.
6. Expand media and digital literacy education, and equip New Zealanders to navigate AI-generated media and other emerging digital technologies.
7. Reduce barriers to digital inclusion and ensure all communities have access to the internet, suitable devices and offline alternatives for essential services.

**Small Business**: *Championing small, local enterprise.* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2026-small-business.md))

1. Revitalise ‘Buy Kiwi Made’ and expand country of origin labelling so it’s easier to support local businesses.
2. Commit government departments to buying more goods and services from Aotearoa businesses.
3. Foster sustainable, low-carbon jobs in the information and communication technology sector by expanding access to grants and rebates for smaller sized firms.
4. Continue to invest in community-led regional development with a focus on sustainable building, regenerative agriculture and horticulture, improving low-carbon infrastructure, and iwi- and hapū-led economic activity.
5. Reform competition laws to create a fairer playing field for small businesses and to benefit consumers. Increase the resources and powers of regulatory agencies to investigate anti-competitive practice.

<a id="pol54653"></a>
**Return the tax rate to 33 percent for New Zealand's biggest corporations**  
`POL54653` · topics: incomes-and-employment, economy, tax-and-income-support, business-support

- **Why:** This party says that multi-national businesses send profits offshore and don't pay the same taxes as local businesses. This increases prices and decreases wages. ### Manifesto 2026 commitments (verbatim)

**Income**: *Liveable incomes made possible through a fair tax system.* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2026-income.md))

1. Reform the Social Security Act to uphold the dignity of those who need support and ensure everyone has a secure income and a decent standard of living. Implement a high-trust operating model at Work and Income.
2. Increase benefits to liveable rates, individualise benefit entitlements and abolish benefit sanctions.
3. Extend ACC to cover income support and treatment for injuries, disability and illnesses regardless of origin.
4. Strengthen Working for Families by boosting the rate, reducing abatements and extending tax credits to families who are out of work.
5. Make income tax settings fair and progressive, by introducing a tax-free threshold, reducing tax rates for low- and middle-income earners, and increasing the top rate of income tax.
6. Introduce a super-rich tax of 2.5% on net wealth over $10 million so that multimillionaires pay their fair share.
7. Overhaul recoverable assistance so that grants are available for urgent needs instead of loans. Work towards writing off existing debt to MSD and ban attachment orders against beneficiaries.

**Workforce rights**: *Employment protections and decent pay for all workers.* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2026-workforce-rights.md))

1. Strengthen worker bargaining power by changing employment law to default union membership. This means people automatically join a union when they start a new job, but can opt out later.
2. Expand the right to strike, including for breaches of collective agreements and political and solidarity reasons.
3. Strengthen employment law to protect all workers’ free time with a right to disconnect. Ensure protection from unwanted contact or surveillance out of working hours.
4. Explore legislating to put workers’ representatives on boards of publicly listed companies.
5. Guarantee annual minimum wage increases that at least keep up with inflation. Pay all publicly funded roles a living wage. Work towards matching the minimum wage to the living wage.
6. Increase paid parental leave to 15 months for the primary caregiver, with additional ring-fenced leave for partners, while also increasing payments.
7. Protect platform and gig-economy workers by strengthening the test for whether a worker is a contractor.
8. Close the gender and ethnic pay gaps by undoing the Government’s changes to the pay equity regime and resuming claims, pay transparency measures, and comprehensive pay gap reporting.

### Manifesto 2026 commitments (verbatim)

**Drug Law Reform**: *Putting health first to keep people safe.* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2026-drug-law-reform.md))

1. Repeal and replace the Misuse of Drugs Act with an evidence-based approach that reduces harm, treats drug use as a health issue and provides for regulated access to cannabis for personal use.
2. Ramp up funding of harm reduction and addiction support for people who want to reduce or stop their drug intake, including through kaupapa Māori, rainbow, youth and harm reduction programmes.
3. Work with local government and service providers — focused on safe drug use, addictions and social housing — to support town centres negatively impacted by drug use.
4. Enable a licensing system for psychedelic treatment and recognise taonga status of our native psylocibin (magic mushroom) species.
5. Pass Good Samaritan laws that allow people to call for help without fear of punishment. Legalise and fund other overdose measures including increasing the availability of naloxone and medically supervised consumption spaces to reduce harm and save lives.
6. Fund culturally responsive vaping and smoking cessation services, phase down nicotine availability, and implement stronger regulation and enforcement for nicotine retailers to protect young people and children.
7. Replace the Land Transport (Drug Driving) Amendment Act 2025 with an impairment approach to reduce harm from all causes of driving impairment.
8. Phase out all alcohol advertising and sponsorship, including at sporting and cultural events, and use funding from the alcohol levy to establish a well-resourced national harm-reduction campaign.

**Health**: *Accessible care to support everyone’s good health.* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2026-health.md))

1. Ensure public health care services are accessible for all with a focus on prevention and early screening, diagnosis and treatment for non-communicable diseases, such as kidney disease, cancers, diabetes and cardiovascular and respiratory diseases.
2. Fund mobile health care and mental health care clinics, diagnostics services and dental vans to ensure rural communities are able to access health services regularly, including during and after civil emergencies.
3. Work towards a publicly delivered, fully free provision of dental and primary care services, including by-Māori for-Māori community clinics.
4. Fund one-stop-shops that provides pā harakeke wrap-around services for whānau throughout hapūtanga, after birth, first stages of life, and navigating parenthood.
5. Stop overly prescriptive Hauora service contracts and commit to working with Iwi Māori Partnership Boards and Hauora Māori to simplify and improve funding arrangements for providers of health services for whānau, hapū iwi and hapori.
6. Increase sustained funding for Pharmac so that it can invest in new medicines and health care devices to enhance treatment outcomes and quality of life.
7. Expand the Minor Health Conditions Service to help pharmacies treat common health issues and update the Integrated community pharmacy services agreement to encourage pharmacists to give appropriate medical advice by compensating them fairly.
8. Ensure all health care workers have fair wages, fund pay parity for primary care nurses and hauora providers, and set safe staffing levels to support worker wellbeing and quality of care for patients.
9. Work towards diagnosing and treating endometriosis faster, including by developing formal clinical guidelines for diagnosing and treating endometriosis and other pelvic pain, and by funding specialised clinics across Aotearoa.
10. Increase funding for data and digital infrastructure and capability in the health sector, and regulate and hold private providers of infrastructure to high standards of privacy.

**Mental Health**: *A safe, supportive and accessible care system.* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2026-mental-health.md))

1. Expand free mental health services to all communities so everyone can access support when they need it. This includes expanding youth services like Piki, Mana Ake and Youth One Stop Shops throughout Aotearoa, Asian Family Services and dedicated support for postnatal mental health.
2. Implement the recommendations of the Every Life Matters – He Tapu te Oranga o ia Tangata Suicide Prevention Strategy, together with further actions identified as part of the kaupapa Māori response to suicide prevention with particular focus on people under 24.
3. Implement community care models and ensure mental health facilities are resourced adequately to enable phasing out the use of seclusion (solitary confinement) entirely, and increase the availability of early intervention to reduce the use of compulsory care.
4. Fund kaupapa Māori mental health and addiction programmes and ensure rangatahi Māori voice is represented in policy.
5. Link primary health and secondary mental health services with clear referral pathways in every health region and focus on areas which have disproportionate need.

<a id="pol54744"></a>

### Manifesto 2026 commitments (verbatim)

**Climate Action: Emissions Reduction**: *Bold action and solutions that hold polluters to account* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2020-climate-action-emissions-reduction.md))

1. Strengthen the Zero Carbon Act by requiring the government Budget process to be consistent with limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees, gross emissions reduction targets and international commitments.
2. Empower the Climate Change Commission to directly set unit supply in the Emissions Trading Scheme, in line with emissions budgets. Align the government Budget process with the National Adaptation Plan and Emissions Reduction Plans.
3. Introduce a price on agricultural emissions to ensure methane reduction targets are met, with financial and technical support for on-farm emissions reduction.
4. Reform the Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS) to restore credibility to the market by phasing out the free allocation of units, removing forestry offsetting so the system functions as a genuine ‘cap-and-trade’ system, and redirecting funding from the reformed ETS to an improved Government Investment in Decarbonising Industry Fund.
5. Ensure Aotearoa meets our Paris Agreement commitments through strong domestic action and, if necessary, environmentally and socially responsible initiatives overseas.
6. Improve public transparency on the costs of inaction by including the fiscal impact of the Nationally Determined Contribution obligation in the financial statements.

**Climate Action: Resilience and Adaption**: *Keeping Aotearoa safe and prepared* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2026-climate-action-resilience-adaptation.md))

1. Ensure climate adaptation planning affirms tino rangatiratanga and upholds the mana motuhake of whānau, hapū and iwi over whenua, wai and taonga by appropriately funding a Māori Climate Resilience Fund.
2. Expand the role of the Natural Hazards Commission to include cover for climate-related weather events and ensure it plays a key role in managing community-led adaptation and retreat.
3. Prioritise long-term, nature-based solutions over short-term engineering solutions, and increase funding for hapū, iwi and community organisations to deliver these.
4. Ensure planning frameworks give effect to the need for climate adaptation in the approach to land and water use, together with supporting ecosystem restoration and conservation.
5. Establish a dedicated fund for central and local government to implement climate adaptation and resilience measures, including funding for partnerships with tangata whenua and community organisations.
6. Scale up support for, and work with, neighbouring countries in the Pacific to adapt to climate change, and advocate for an international agreement on the rights of people displaced by climate change.

**Conservation and Biodiversity**: *Protecting and restoring plants, animals and ecosystems.* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2026-conservation-and-biodiversity.md))

1. Reform conservation and wildlife protection laws to give effect to Te Tiriti, elevate Indigenous-led land stewardship and ensure the conservation management system prioritises halting and reversing nature loss in Aotearoa.
2. Ban new mining on conservation land, including stewardship land.
3. Expand funding for Jobs for Nature – Mahi mō te Taiao to protect our biodiversity and create thousands of regional jobs.
4. Protect all remaining natural wetlands in legislation, including coastal wetlands and estuaries, and implement a plan to restore at least 30% of degraded wetland area, prioritising areas most important for biodiversity recovery and community resilience.
5. Fund Action for Nature, the implementation plan for the biodiversity strategy, and implement national guidance to protect indigenous biodiversity, including the protection of taonga species.
6. Increase overall public conservation funding, including increasing funding and support for the Predator Free 2050 goal.

**Energy**: *Powering Aotearoa with affordable renewable energy.* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2026-energy.md))

1. Put public wellbeing outcomes first in legislation to guarantee the power system works for people, not profits.
2. Establish a renewable energy infrastructure agency to ensure security of supply and lower prices for households, businesses and industry.
3. Increase resilience by enabling greater distributed solar and batteries for households, marae and suitable public buildings, and supporting community-led energy planning.
4. Ban new fossil fuel extraction, end subsidies for fossil fuels and cancel the LNG terminal.
5. Establish a single energy regulator and a Ministry for Energy, focusing on affordable, secure and sustainable energy with equitable access and Te Tiriti-based frameworks that enable Māori and community involvement, ownership and leadership in energy projects.
6. Work with industry to decarbonise and encourage demand response and energy efficiency.

**Environmental Protection**: *Protecting and restoring nature.* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2026-environmental-protection.md))

1. Implement strong evidence-based limits for ecosystem health, secure the role of Te Tiriti and affirm the role of tangata whenua as shared decision-makers and kaitiaki in the new resource management system.
2. Repeal the Fast-track Approvals Act and revoke consents for fast-track approvals for new coal, gold and seabed mining projects.
3. Restore a standalone Ministry for the Environment. Increase resources for the Environmental Protection Authority to identify risks to the environment and human health, and for compliance, monitoring and enforcement to ensure polluters are held accountable.
4. Update air quality standards to bring Aotearoa in line with international standards and to protect human health.
5. Work towards eradication of biosecurity incursions, specifically wilding pines, Caulerpa, and yellow-legged hornets.
6. Re-establish resources for the Community Environment Fund to support grassroots environmental education and action.

**Food Fibre and Forestry**: *A regenerative approach that puts people and nature first.* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2026-food-fibre-and-forestry.md))

1. Increase support for farmers to transition to more sustainable forms of agricultural production through finance mechanisms such as low-interest loans and grants.
2. Back Aotearoa-grown natural fibres, including wool, by using them in the construction and refurbishment of schools and public buildings, and establishing a contestable fund for sustainable fibre manufacturing and innovation.
3. Ban palm kernel expeller and ensure all supplementary feed is sustainably sourced and does not strain the carrying capacity of the local environment.
4. Prevent land from being used beyond its capacities by implementing strong controls on clear-fell of plantation forestry, working to transition extremely erosion-prone land to indigenous forestry and establishing a National Soil Strategy that sets direction on soil use, policies and research.
5. Support the local wood processing sector to manufacture higher-value timber products from plantation forestry, such as cross-laminated timber for construction and turning slash into solid biofuels, retaining regional employment and development.
6. Work with Māori-led forestry organisations to support investment in forestry and restoration of forests on whenua Māori and recognise tangata whenua customary use rights in indigenous forestry according to their tīkanga.
7. Establish a biodiversity credits scheme that supports landowners to undertake restoration and protection of land as a voluntary revenue alternative to the Emissions Trading Scheme. As part of this, prioritise marginal whenua Māori where agreed by landowners.

**Freshwater**: *Healthy water for drinking, swimming and gathering kai.* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2026-freshwater.md))

1. Implement strong, evidence-based national bottom lines for freshwater for both human health and ecosystem health to address pollution including lowering the nitrate limit for drinking water.
2. Reinstate Te Mana o Te Wai to prioritise the health of freshwater in decision-making and regulation and to give effect to Te Tiriti o Waitangi.
3. End all subsidies and public funding for big new irrigation and dam projects and review resource consents where water levels have dropped too far to support a healthy river.
4. Strengthen environmental performance rules for wastewater discharges to ensure lakes, rivers, beaches and coastal areas remain swimmable.
5. Ensure the drinking water regulator is funded and given the mandate for robust and transparent monitoring, reporting and enforcement in the protection of drinking water sources.
6. Support greater resilience from floods by increasing funding for adaptation and allowing for a ‘room for rivers’ approach and using natural systems like wetlands to protect communities.
7. Phase out synthetic nitrogen fertiliser and take action to reduce stocking rates on a catchment basis to improve the health of rivers and drinking water and reduce climate pollution.

**Oceans and Fisheries**: *Abundant oceans teeming with kaimoana.* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2026-oceans-and-fisheries.md))

1. Protect at least 30% of New Zealand’s ocean territory by 2030 through reforming marine protected areas legislation to ensure it is fit for purpose and enables both tikanga-led tools consistent with Te Tiriti, and approaches to improve ocean health outcomes.
2. Phase out damaging fishing methods, starting by banning bottom trawling on seamounts, and banning set netting and dredging.
3. Ban seabed mining in the coastal marine area and the exclusive economic zone and maintain pressure for a moratorium on seabed mining in international waters.
4. Embed kaitiakitanga Māori in marine policy and operational management. Resource iwi and hapū to lead oceans protection and implement mātauranga- and tikanga-based projects for ocean conservation.
5. Reduce fisheries bycatch of protected species by ensuring cameras are rolled out on the entire fishing fleet and by setting fisheries-related mortality limits.
6. Ratify the Agreement on Marine Biological Diversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction and support marine protection proposals in the high seas, Southern Ocean and throughout the Pacific.
7. Review the Quota Management System and move towards an ecosystem-based fisheries management model, in line with the Māori fisheries settlements.

**Welfare of Animals**: *Caring for all animals that call Aotearoa home.* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2026-welfare-of-animals.md))

1. Create a new Commissioner for Animals to independently monitor and advocate for the rights of animals, and an independent ministry.
2. Resource the National Animal Welfare Advisory Committee to ensure all animal welfare codes genuinely comply with the Animal Welfare Act, and introduce stronger codes for farmed animals.
3. Phase out harmful activities including debeaking of hens, intensive winter grazing, factory farming, octopus farming, farrowing crates and rodeo.
4. Require that imported products meet the animal welfare standards of Aotearoa, including for cosmetics.
5. Introduce consistent, clear and enforceable standards for manufacturing claims about animal welfare and ingredients (such as ‘free range’, ‘cruelty free’ and ‘vegan’).
6. Retain the ban on live exports of farmed animals by sea and extend the ban to include live exports of farmed animals by air and wild-caught animals such as endangered tuna longfin eels.

**Zero Waste**: *Building a sustainable circular economy.* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2026-zero-waste.md))

1. Establish strong product policy measures, including mandatory product stewardship, a beverage container return scheme, phase-outs of problematic products and comprehensive right-to-repair.
2. Direct revenue from the waste disposal levy into waste minimisation initiatives and stop diverting the local government portion to other purposes. Increase the levy to match international best practice and apply a consistent rate across all landfill classes.
3. Introduce a moratorium on waste-to-energy plants and explore energy generation from biogas associated with animal and plant wastes.
4. Build on proposed reforms of the Waste Minimisation Act to implement timely, binding, measurable and ambitious waste reduction targets. Ensure legislation gives effect to Te Tiriti o Waitangi. Introduce comprehensive duty-of-care systems for the waste and resource recovery sector covering all waste streams, including hazardous waste.
5. Make greater use of discarded soil. Divert soil from landfills, where safe and appropriate to do so.
6. Prioritise local, mana whenua and community-driven solutions to resource recovery, implementation of national zero-waste strategies, and organic waste reduction, diversion and processing.

`POL54766` · topics: transport-and-infrastructure, economy, energy, economic-development-and-industry

- **Why:** This party says that NZ needs a resilient energy system to provide backup renewable power that keeps electricity affordable when hydro lakes are low and wind power decreases. Gas historically fills this gap, but gas is being exhausted more quickly than expected.

### Manifesto 2026 commitments (verbatim)

**Transport**: *Easy, sustainable ways to get around.* ([full chapter](documents/web-manifesto-2026-transport.md))

1. Transform public transport networks, including building mass rapid transit in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch, and providing comprehensive bus lanes in all cities.
2. Invest in nationwide rapid rail for passengers and freight to connect regions and major cities and contribute to economic development and decarbonisation.
3. Introduce targeted subsidies for e-cargo bikes. Introduce e-bike sharing schemes in community hubs, to allow more families to save on transport costs.
4. Fund affordable, reliable, interregional rural bus services, and on-demand public transport, including by-Māori for-Māori public transport to serve kōhanga reo and rural schools.
5. Extend Community Connect to provide free fares for students and apprentices, community service card holders, everyone under 18, and all Total Mobility card holders.
6. Enable the provision of transport services publicly instead of for profit by replacing the Public Transport Operating Model.
7. Create safe walking and biking routes to all community hubs including schools through building more bike lanes and safe crossings, and lowering speed limits near schools.
8. Implement a phase-out date for the import of fossil-fuel powered vehicles, build more EV (electric vehicle) charging stations, remove regulatory barriers to EV car-sharing and re-introduce incentives for EV uptake.
