`POL55322` · topics: law-justice-and-government, criminal-justice · summary: policy.nz

- **Why:** This party says that the "right to silence" is a fundamental part of the judicial system where people can choose not to speak in a court case if they do not wish to. #### Require retirement villages to pay out house sales within nine months

`POL55089` · topics: community-and-inclusion, seniors, key-policies-community-and-inclusion · summary: policy.nz

- **Why:** This party says that older New Zealanders need the balance in relationships with retirement village companies to shift more towards residents. #### Increase sentence lengths for murder (POL55355)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that the criminal justice system needs to prioritise victims over perpetrators. **How** (*policy.nz*): This party would introduce a formal degree of murder regime whereby first degree murder is life imprisonment without a chance of parole; second degree murder is an aggravated life sentence with a minimum sentence of non-parole period of 30 years. The party would also increase sentences for attempted murder and wounding with intent to cause grievous bodily harm from 14 years to 25 years. It would increase the standard parole eligibility to 75% of a sentence for long-term offenders so that those convicted of murder have to be assessed as having a low probability of reoffending before release. It would also limit sentence discounts for factors other than a guilty plea to 10%. Guilty plea discounts will remain limited to 25%.

## Method & sources

1. Started from policy.nz's NZ First data (`raw/policy.nz/parties/nz-first.json`): statement, Why/How, citations.
2. nzfirst.nz blocks automated access (Cloudflare 403, also with a headless browser) and web.archive.org is unreachable from this environment. The party's own web pages were therefore recovered from **Common Crawl**: its 2026 crawl indexes (CC-MAIN-2026-12 … -43) were searched for every nzfirst.nz URL and the latest HTTP-200 capture of each page was read from the WARC archive on data.commoncrawl.org (`tools/policies_nzf_tpm_cc_index.py`, `tools/policies_nzf_tpm_cc_fetch.py`). Each such document (`documents/site-*.md`) records the capture date and WARC record; captures date from 2026-07-19 to 2026-10-14, so later edits are not reflected.
3. In addition, every New Zealand First press release and speech from late 2025 to 23 Oct 2026 was collected from Scoop's organisation page (https://info.scoop.co.nz/New_Zealand_First_Party); Scoop republishes party releases as issued, so their text is the party's own. Policy PDFs the party attached to releases (img.scoop.co.nz) or linked from its site (Google Drive) were downloaded and text-extracted.
4. Each policy links (a) the page policy.nz cited (now mostly a Common Crawl capture) and (b) other party texts on the same policy. Where a cited page could not be recovered at all, a `documents/not-retrieved-*.md` file records the URL and the reason; it contains no paraphrase.
5. Policies found in party texts but missing from policy.nz were added with neutral summaries (`summary_source: archive`). Calls on the current government and positions (e.g. opposing a bill) are included where the party presents them as what it stands for, and are labelled as such.

### POL54754: Increase the milk quantity guaranteed to NZ dairy manufacturing

**Statement:** Increase the milk quantity guaranteed to NZ dairy manufacturing  
*Summary source: policy.nz* · topics: economy, agriculture, trade-and-exports, economic-development-and-industry

- **Why:** This party says that the present 50 million litres per year is too low to incentivise production at a large scale. The status-quo supports New Zealand-based dairy manufacturers, but does not support these firms to scale to size, which disincentives investment into Fonterra. 

Marketing ‘New Zealand Dairy’, this party sees this policy as a means of making NZ’s dairy manufacturing sector more competitive in export markets. It says it is important for the milk provision not to be a subsidy; dairy manufacturing firms would cover delivery and collection costs and pay farmers market rates.
- **How:** This party would increase milk access from 50 million litres to 500 million litres per year over the first six years. From there, access would taper to 80 per cent, 60 per cent, 40 per cent and 20 per cent to encourage immediate investment. This would be done through changing the Dairy Industry Restructuring Act 2001.

### POL54964: Remove automatic work rights from student visas

**Statement:** Remove automatic work rights from student visas  
*Summary source: policy.nz* · topics: education, migration, incomes-and-employment, tertiary-fees-and-student-support, wages-and-working-conditions

- **Why:** This party says that student visa holders compete in the competitive graduate job market and can take jobs from New Zealanders. It stays the intent of international education is for overseas economies to give money to NZ by paying for their education, not to provide automatic work rights and residence pathways. The party also cites broader concern with net numbers of migrants entering New Zealand and sees changes to student visas as a way of reducing net migration and its effect on infrastructure.

## Law & order

### NZF-A08: 'Life means life': degrees of murder, whole-of-life sentences for first-degree murder and child rape

**Statement:** 'Life means life': degrees of murder, whole-of-life sentences for first-degree murder and child rape  
*Summary source: archive* · topics: criminal-justice, law-justice-and-government

- **Why:** The party says the justice system too often fails to hold offenders to account and victims should come before offenders.
- **How:** This party would create a formal 'degrees of murder' regime (1st degree: life without parole; 2nd degree: minimum non-parole period of 30 years; 3rd degree: minimum 10 years), increase sentences for attempted murder and wounding with intent from 14 to 25 years, and introduce life imprisonment for rape of children.
- **Sources:**
  - [NZFirst Law And Order Policy Announcement: Tougher Sentences, Degrees Of Murder, Smashing Organised Crime (Press release, 2026-10-22)](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00200/nzfirst-law-and-order-policy-announcement-tougher-sentences-degrees-of-murder-smashing-organised-crime.htm) — [full text](documents/2026-10-22-nzfirst-law-and-order-policy-announcement-tougher-sentences.md)

### NZF-A09: More mandatory minimum sentences, tougher parole and limits on sentence discounts

**Statement:** More mandatory minimum sentences, tougher parole and limits on sentence discounts  
*Summary source: archive* · topics: criminal-justice

- **Why:** The party says sentencing has not delivered justice for victims.
- **How:** This party would increase the use of mandatory minimum sentences for serious violent and sexual offenders, cap non-guilty-plea discounts at 10% (guilty-plea discounts stay at 25%), raise parole eligibility to 75% of the sentence for long-term offenders, require murderers to be assessed as low risk before release, set an 8-year minimum non-parole period for 'coward punch' killings, treat home burglary like aggravated burglary, and oppose any extension of the Clean Slate law.
- **Sources:**
  - [NZFirst Law And Order Policy Announcement: Tougher Sentences, Degrees Of Murder, Smashing Organised Crime (Press release, 2026-10-22)](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00200/nzfirst-law-and-order-policy-announcement-tougher-sentences-degrees-of-murder-smashing-organised-crime.htm) — [full text](documents/2026-10-22-nzfirst-law-and-order-policy-announcement-tougher-sentences.md)

### NZF-A10: Create a dedicated organised-crime agency and fold the Serious Fraud Office into Police

**Statement:** Create a dedicated organised-crime agency and fold the Serious Fraud Office into Police  
*Summary source: archive* · topics: criminal-justice, public-sector

- **Why:** The party says transnational organised crime is growing and needs to be dismantled.
- **How:** This party would establish a dedicated agency, with a responsible minister, to dismantle transnational criminal networks, ensure Police have the resources they need, and abolish the SFO, replacing it with a specialised division inside NZ Police.
- **Sources:**
  - [NZFirst Law And Order Policy Announcement: Tougher Sentences, Degrees Of Murder, Smashing Organised Crime (Press release, 2026-10-22)](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00200/nzfirst-law-and-order-policy-announcement-tougher-sentences-degrees-of-murder-smashing-organised-crime.htm) — [full text](documents/2026-10-22-nzfirst-law-and-order-policy-announcement-tougher-sentences.md)

### NZF-A11: Strengthen self-defence protections, including investigating 'Castle Doctrine' laws

**Statement:** Strengthen self-defence protections, including investigating 'Castle Doctrine' laws  
*Summary source: archive* · topics: criminal-justice, family-justice-and-safety

- **Why:** The party says people should be able to defend themselves and their property in their home or business.
- **How:** This party would investigate 'Castle Doctrine' and 'Stand Your Ground' laws (no duty to retreat), change Police and Solicitor-General prosecution guidelines so people who 'excessively defend' themselves at home or work are treated as victims unless there is overwhelming contrary evidence, and require the Solicitor-General to review any such prosecution.
- **Sources:**
  - [NZFirst Law And Order Policy Announcement: Tougher Sentences, Degrees Of Murder, Smashing Organised Crime (Press release, 2026-10-22)](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00200/nzfirst-law-and-order-policy-announcement-tougher-sentences-degrees-of-murder-smashing-organised-crime.htm) — [full text](documents/2026-10-22-nzfirst-law-and-order-policy-announcement-tougher-sentences.md)

**Statement:** State-funded immediate reparation for victims, faster publication of sentencing notes, less name suppression  
*Summary source: archive* · topics: criminal-justice, civil-justice

- **Why:** The party says victims should come first and the courts should be more open.

### POL54661: Return at least 50 percent of mining project royalties to the region where mining took place

**Statement:** Return at least 50 percent of mining project royalties to the region where mining took place  
*Summary source: policy.nz* · topics: economy, te-ao-maori, oil-gas-and-mining, economic-development-and-industry, regional-development, land-and-resources

- **Why:** This party says that mining plays a vital role in NZ's economy and regions as one of the country's most productive sectors. The benefits of mining do not always stay in these regions, and communities should directly benefit from local mining projects. If mining expands, infrastructure and development in the regions must grow too.
- **How:** This party would invest 50 percent of mining royalties in the region the resources were extracted from. This money would also fund Mines Rescue capabilities.

# New Zealand Loyal (NZ Loyal) — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **New Zealand Loyal (NZ Loyal)** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **10 policies** listed, backed by **1 full-text source document** and 1 documented-as-unretrievable source.

- Party website: <https://nzloyal.com/>
- Registration: 5 August 2026 (re-registered; Electoral Commission register)

## About this list

NZ Loyal (leader Kelvyn Alp) was re-registered in August 2026. **Its own policy pages could not be captured**: nzloyal.com is behind a Cloudflare bot challenge that blocked both curl and a headless browser. The only verbatim party wording available to this archive is a ten-point list RNZ quoted from the party's website on 12 October 2026; each point is listed below with that RNZ article as the source.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/nz-loyal/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). # NZ Outdoors & Freedom Party ('freedom') — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **NZ Outdoors & Freedom Party ('freedom')** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **18 policies** listed, backed by **12 full-text source documents**.

- Party website: <https://freedom.kiwi/ (registered as www.nzofp.co.nz, which serves the same site)>
- Registration: 11 August 2017 (Electoral Commission register)

## About this list

The NZ Outdoors & Freedom Party (leader Sue Grey) now brands itself 'freedom'. Its Policies page links ten policy pages: Direct Democracy (its 'new core pillar'), Agriculture, Housing, Open Source First, Cannabis, Anti-Bullying, the ACC Justice & Accountability statement, Education, Fisheries, and Outdoors Recreation & Wildlife. Each distinct commitment on those pages is listed below.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/nz-outdoors-freedom/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). Party claims (costs, statistics) are reported as the party's claims, not verified.

**Gaps and caveats.** The home page renders almost no text without JavaScript (captured as-is). Pages are undated; costings appear only in the ACC statement. Positions on 1080, fluoride and 5G described in media coverage were not found on the current policy pages, so are not listed.

## Headline policies

- [Entrench the NZ Bill of Rights Act as supreme law](#entrench-the-nz-bill-of-rights-act-as-supreme-law-ofp-01) — Law, justice & government
- [Introduce Swiss-style binding citizens' referendums: a citizens' veto on laws and citizen-initiated laws](#introduce-swiss-style-binding-citizens-referendums-a-citizens-veto-on-laws-and-citizen-initiated-laws-ofp-02) — Law, justice & government
- [Withdraw from the Paris Agreement and focus on flood management and carbon-rich soils](#withdraw-from-the-paris-agreement-and-focus-on-flood-management-and-carbon-rich-soils-ofp-04) — Environment
- [Replace DOC with a Department of Outdoors – Wildlife, Recreation & Nature (DOWRN)](#replace-doc-with-a-department-of-outdoors--wildlife-recreation--nature-dowrn-ofp-18) — Environment

## Contents by topic

- [Defence & foreign affairs](#defence--foreign-affairs) (1)
- [Economy](#economy) (2)
- [Education](#education) (2)
- [Environment](#environment) (3)
- [Health](#health) (4)
- [Housing](#housing) (3)
- [Law, justice & government](#law-justice--government) (3)

## Defence & foreign affairs

### Leave the CPTPP (TPPA) and RCEP and pursue 'fair trade' bilateral deals (OFP-06)

**How** (*archive*): Withdraw from agreements that limit New Zealand's ability to legislate, increase Pacific trade, strengthen anti-monopoly law and place a moratorium on sales of farmland, forestry, housing and infrastructure to non-tax-residents.

Full text: [Agriculture Policy](documents/agriculture-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/agriculture-policy))

## Economy

### Adopt an 'Open Source First' rule for government software procurement (OFP-10)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says dependence on multinational software vendors is a hidden import cost and a resilience risk.

**How** (*archive*): Agencies must check for a suitable open-source option before buying proprietary software, compare whole-of-life costs, and use New Zealand providers for support.

Full text: [Open Source First: Keeping New Zealand' s Digital Wealth in New Zealand](documents/open-source-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/open-source-policy))

### Replace the fisheries Quota Management System with a LegaSea-style system keeping fisheries in public ownership (OFP-17)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says the QMS has depleted fish stocks, privatised a public resource and priced locals out.

**How** (*archive*): Tendered commercial permits with no private sale of fishing rights, catches landed and processed in NZ, only NZ-owned operators, fleet separation in the territorial sea, and more recreational and customary inshore access.

Full text: [Fisheries Policy](documents/nzofp-fisheries-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/nzofp-fisheries-policy))

## Education

### Make early childhood centres and primary schools Wi-Fi free, using wired connections (OFP-15)

**How** (*archive*): Minimise Wi-Fi in high schools too and work with Chorus on wired fibre connections.

Full text: [Education Policy](documents/education-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/education-policy))

### Invest heavily in education with an outdoors- and community-focused curriculum, implementing the Tomorrow's Schools Review (OFP-16)

Full text: [Education Policy](documents/education-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/education-policy))

## Environment

### Withdraw from the Paris Agreement and focus on flood management and carbon-rich soils (OFP-04)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says farm animals cannot release more carbon than they eat and that extreme weather is 'nature, not climate change'.

**How** (*archive*): Exit Paris (it says staying would cost more than leaving), maintain river flows and channels to reduce flood risk, and support ecological agriculture with minimal synthetic inputs.

Full text: [Agriculture Policy](documents/agriculture-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/agriculture-policy))

### Replace the EPA with an independent Health-Environment Protection Agency and apply the precautionary principle to new technology (OFP-05)

**How** (*archive*): New technologies and products only with full liability for the business introducing them; independent biosecurity at every entry point.

Full text: [Agriculture Policy](documents/agriculture-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/agriculture-policy))

### Replace DOC with a Department of Outdoors – Wildlife, Recreation & Nature (DOWRN) (OFP-18)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says governments have undervalued New Zealanders' outdoors culture and access.

**How** (*archive*): A department promoting access to all public land, coasts and rivers, poison-free conservation (trapping rather than poisons), food gathering on public land, and early public engagement on access decisions.

Full text: [Recreation & Wildlife Policy](documents/outdoors-recreation-and-wildlife-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/outdoors-recreation-and-wildlife-policy))

## Health

### Decriminalise personal cannabis use and cultivation and support medicinal cannabis and hemp (OFP-11)

**How** (*archive*): No criminal offence for personal possession or growing; support home-grown medicinal cannabis and small NZ suppliers over 'Big Pharma', with lower licensing barriers; update law to support hemp products.

Full text: [Cannabis Policy](documents/cannabis-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/cannabis-policy))

### Create a nationwide anti-bullying strategy treating bullying as a public-health issue (OFP-12)

**How** (*archive*): Awareness programmes in schools and communities, leadership training for teachers and managers, bullying questions in routine health screening, and treatment of psychological effects.

Full text: [Anti Bullying Policy](documents/anti-bullying-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/anti-bullying-policy))

### Make one doctor's injury diagnosis final for ACC and abolish ACC's review and dispute machinery (OFP-13)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says ACC 'expert shopping' is used to decline claims.

**How** (*archive*): Disestablish ACC review specialists and investigators, cancel contracts with FairWay and ICRA, stop paying external consultants to contest diagnoses; it claims $61.5m a year savings to redirect to surgery, rehabilitation and disability support.

Full text: [ACC Policy Statement](documents/the-acc-justice-accountability-policy-statement.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/the-acc-justice-accountability-policy-statement))

### Pursue Pfizer for breach of contract over Covid-19 vaccines and recover ACC vaccine-injury costs (OFP-14)

**How** (*archive*): Release the full NZ Pfizer contract, bring a Crown claim to recover the $16.8m ACC has paid for vaccine injuries, guarantee ACC compensation for long-term vaccine harm, give ACC a statutory right of recourse against manufacturers, and review ACC law to cover distress and loss of enjoyment of life.

Full text: [ACC Policy Statement](documents/the-acc-justice-accountability-policy-statement.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/the-acc-justice-accountability-policy-statement))

## Housing

### Free up land and revise the RMA to speed house building, with a mix of public and private housing (OFP-07)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says every citizen should have access to an affordable, warm, dry home.

**How** (*archive*): Identify land for subdivision, sequence servicing and construction, and have the Ministry of Housing take a hands-on role.

Full text: [Housing Policy](documents/housing-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/housing-policy))

### Require high standards for new homes (R5 insulation, rainwater and greywater systems, energy efficiency) and fund hempcrete building (OFP-08)

**How** (*archive*): Also solar or micro-generation, green space for gardens, recycling of building materials, lower consent costs for sustainable materials, and a funding scheme for hempcrete homes.

Full text: [Housing Policy](documents/housing-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/housing-policy))

### Fully fund night shelters and low-cost living spaces for homeless people (OFP-09)

**How** (*archive*): Shelters would provide two nutritious meals a day and supplements; the party also wants to restore New Zealand's leadership in social housing.

## About this list

Opportunity (leader Qiulae Wong) publishes its platform as 15 policy pages (priority policies: Abundant Energy, Breakthrough Economy, Clean Up Politics, Healthy Oceans, Tax Reset; plus Citizens' Voice, Future-fit Education, Healthy People, Honouring Te Tiriti, Smart on Crime, Affordable Housing, Digital Future, Inter-Generational Infrastructure, Climate Action, Healthy Land & Water), most with a downloadable PDF policy paper, plus statements and five election "bottom lines". The list below starts from policy.nz's 56 statements for the party (with policy.nz's own Why/How text) and adds policies from TOP's documents that policy.nz does not list (IDs OPP-A..).

**How the text was obtained.** www.opportunity.org.nz is behind a Cloudflare bot challenge (HTTP 403 to curl and headless Chromium) and web.archive.org is unreachable from this environment, so web pages were recovered from **Common Crawl** WARC captures (crawls CC-MAIN-2026-30/34/39/43; capture date in each document's front matter) via [`tools/policies_minor_cc.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_cc.py). The 15 policy PDFs were downloaded directly from cdn.opportunity.org.nz (not blocked). Press releases are also taken from their scoop.co.nz mirrors.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/opportunity/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

Summaries marked *policy.nz* are policy.nz's neutral "This party says…" text, reproduced unchanged. Summaries marked *archive* were written for this archive from the linked full text: one to three neutral sentences; "Why" is the party's own stated reason, "How" what it says it would do.

**Gaps and caveats.** Three pages cited by policy.nz have no Common Crawl capture and could not be retrieved: /healthy_land (Healthy Land & Water policy — water quality, gene technology context), /disability_statement and /arts_and_culture_statement; their documents say so explicitly, and the policy.nz summaries are kept. Common Crawl captures date from July–October 2026 and may predate later edits. Note that the Citizens' Voice PDF is dated June 2025. The NZ Herald reported (Oct 2026) that tax reform is not among TOP's five bottom lines; the Tax Reset remains on its policy page. Web search capacity ran out during research, so further Scoop mirrors were not sought.

### Improved respite and carer support for the disabled (POL55267)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says accessibility and care is a growing issue. One in six Kiwis have a disability and if ageing-related access issues are factored in, 1 in 4 Kiwis will have accessibility needs in their lifetimes. Everyone should be able to participate in society with dignity and make the most of opportunities. However, the current Disability Support Services Bill did not properly consult with those it affects, and fails to give paid and unpaid carers the support they deserve.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would look to improve disability policy, including good care plans for disabled adults as their family carers age. It would back pay equity for care and support workers. It would also seek more support for unpaid carers, with improved respite care and more flexibility to balance their employment and unpaid caring roles.

### Oppose disabled people being paid less than minimum wage (POL55269)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that many disabled people lose benefit income if they work and some are even legally paid less than the minimum wage. One in six Kiwis are disabled and when ageing-related access issues are factored in, one in four Kiwis will face access issues in their lifetimes. So access to care and income are key issues for those with disabilities.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would work to end rules that allow disabled people to be paid less than the minimum wage. It would improve support for employers to recruit and retain disabled workers. This party argues its Citizens’ Income and Disability Allowance would ensure disabled people would not lose income support for doing paid work.

### Ensure better connections between government systems and those with a disability (POL55271)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says people with long-term disabilities often find themselves endlessly repeating their story or having to prove their disability to authorities. Or they may fall through the cracks if their health, education, ACC and disability support systems are not strongly connected.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would back a "Tell Us Once" system, which would mean those with long-term disability support needs would not have to repeat their story or have tests over and over. ## Education

### Forgive student loan interest for returning Kiwis (POL54852)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says our economy needs new ideas and science, technology and innovation are traditional sources for fresh thinking. The country needs young talented Kiwis who are currently offshore to bring their experience and skills back to help drive the economy.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would roll back the student loan interest of returning Kiwis on up to 3 years spent overseas. This would apply to both newly graduates and those currently overseas. The rollback would be applied at the end of their loan repayment, and conditional on being resident in New Zealand when the loan is repaid. This policy would cost an estimated $95m.

## Environment

### Phase out inshore bottom-trawling by 2030 and make fishing more sustainable (POL54776)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that our seas are hitting their ecological and economic limits. Fish species are being depleted under the current quota management system, and critical habitats are unprotected. Just 0.5% of NZ’s extensive ocean territory is protected as a marine reserve.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would change the fisheries management system and make it more transparent. This includes the phasing out bottom trawling in all inshore areas by 2030 and installing cameras on commercial fishing boats. It would also move away from single-species quotas towards an ecosystem-based approach, and raise the baseline for sustainable fish stocks. 
In the short-term, the party says its wider oceans policy would cost no more than $100m a year, with some costs recovered from the commercial fishing industry.

## Housing

### Introduce a land value tax of 1.75 percent (POL54777)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that the current tax system is outdated and does not address the cost-of-living crisis, unaffordable housing, and the increasing pressure of the superannuation system. Under its tax plan, this party says incomes will increase for 70 percent of New Zealanders, and another 20% will see no change.

**How** (*policy.nz*): An annual land value tax of 1.75 percent on urban land - and 0.5% on rural land - would be part of a wider tax reset aimed at incomes, house prices and retirement savings. The land value tax would lower house prices an estimated 10-15 percent and discourage land-banking and large property portfolios. There would be potential exemptions for farmers, retirees and other "land rich, cash poor" land owners. 
This tax would fund a universal citizen's income, with an extra $4bn for other uses. The tax system would also be simplified, with the number of tax brackets reduced to three - 28 percent, 34 percent and 39 percent

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would select, at random, groups of ordinary people who would serve for a year. The number of people would mirror the number of MPs. They would be compensated for their time and listen to experts, organisations and affected parties on topics that politicians have struggled to find consensus on. The assemblies would work to find common ground and set the policy direction for the politicians to respond to. 
This policy could cost $10-$15m a year, depending on how many assemblies are held.

## Media, culture & recreation

### Provide more support for the arts through a citizens income and innovation funding (POL55323)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that a stronger arts ecosystem creates jobs and wellbeing, builds healthier communities and helps define national identity. NZ sits in the bottom ten OECD countries for public arts investment. The barriers for artists are less about a lack of arts funding and more about unpredictable income, and changing a mindset that the arts are a key part of the economy, rather than an optional extra.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would address the precarity of an artist's income firstly with its universal citizen’s income policy, which would enable artists to take a financial gamble on their career. Tax reforms would help over irregular income and free up charitable giving by repealing the cap on charitable donations. This party would more broadly support the arts through other policies such as an AI framework and revamp of the polytech sector, which would address copyright exploitation and recognise the arts in innovation funding.

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says encouraging businesses to buy electric vehicles will reduce their ongoing fuel costs and make them more resilient to volatile prices. As businesses are big buyers of new vehicles, this would also increase the pool of EVs in the secondhand market.

### Help industries decarbonise with a new fund (POL54900)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that electrification of industry is being blocked by the cost of plant capital, grid connection and network upgrades. Industry has been hampered by a fall in gas reserves and the scrapping of GIDI, a government industry decarbonisation fund. A replacement loan guarantee scheme has fallen short because it cannot overcome the upfront cost, debt constraints and investment risks. This party says money collected from selling carbon units should be used to fight climate pollution, not disappear into the government's consolidated fund.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would establish a ring-fenced Industry Energy Resilience Fund (IERF) which would cover capital and upgrade costs. The fund will be capitalised by a $1b green bond raised against forecast ETS auction revenues over the next decade. 
IERF will offer a greater mix of instruments than GIDI , with grants reserved for smaller targeted uses. 
Money collected from selling carbon units would be used to fight climate change, putting it into IERF by law so businesses could plan ahead.

# Progressive Aotearoa New Zealand (Progressive Party, PPANZ) — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **Progressive Aotearoa New Zealand (Progressive Party, PPANZ)** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **14 policies** listed, backed by **2 full-text source documents**.

- Party website: <https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/>
- Registration: Not a registered party; electorate candidates only (Nelson: Bruce Dyer; West Coast-Tasman: Kevin Rooke; Kāpiti: Michael Walker — per policy.nz)

## About this list

The Progressive Party (PPANZ) publishes a 'Policies' page with sections on health, housing, education, justice, Māori policy, animals and plants, agriculture, climate change, industry, taxation and social boards, each beginning 'The Progressive Party advocates…', plus a longer 'PPANZ Manifesto' (marked as a work in progress, including a Covid-19 strategy white paper). The main advocated positions are listed below.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/progressive-aotearoa-new-zealand/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). Party claims (costs, statistics) are reported as the party's claims, not verified.

**Gaps and caveats.** Undated pages; no costings. The manifesto is captured in full but its points largely repeat the Policies page.

## Headline policies

- [Guarantee access to food, clothing, housing, education and healthcare](#guarantee-access-to-food-clothing-housing-education-and-healthcare-ppa-01) — Community & inclusion
- [Offer state-funded mortgages, a state-owned house-building enterprise and limit home ownership to NZ residents](#offer-state-funded-mortgages-a-state-owned-house-building-enterprise-and-limit-home-ownership-to-nz-residents-ppa-04) — Housing
- [Run businesses with more than nine employees as worker co-operatives and state-manage monopolistic key industries](#run-businesses-with-more-than-nine-employees-as-worker-co-operatives-and-state-manage-monopolistic-key-industries-ppa-12) — Economy

## Contents by topic

- [Community & inclusion](#community--inclusion) (1)
- [Economy](#economy) (2)
- [Education](#education) (1)
- [Environment](#environment) (2)
- [Health](#health) (2)
- [Housing](#housing) (1)
- [Incomes & employment](#incomes--employment) (1)
- [Law, justice & government](#law-justice--government) (2)
- [Te ao Māori](#te-ao-māori) (2)

## Community & inclusion

### Guarantee access to food, clothing, housing, education and healthcare (PPA-01)

**Why** (*archive*): The Progressive Party says economic and political power should serve people rather than concentrated wealth (its stated philosophy draws on economic democracy and 'neohumanism').

**How** (*archive*): Listed in the health, housing and education sections as guarantees for everyone.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

## Economy

### Shift farming to co-operatives and plant-based protein (PPA-10)

**How** (*archive*): Incentivise farmers to move to plant protein (including lab-grown meat) and regenerative, ethical farming models; co-operatives at all levels of agriculture.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

### Run businesses with more than nine employees as worker co-operatives and state-manage monopolistic key industries (PPA-12)

**How** (*archive*): A Minister, Ministry and Centre for Cooperative Studies; railways, power and mining state-managed; a nationwide co-operative supermarket to cut living costs.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

## Education

### Move schooling from national standards to child-centred, experiential learning including meditation and mindfulness (PPA-07)

**How** (*archive*): Learning based on each child's needs, parents as active partners, restorative behaviour management and a Hauora (holistic wellbeing) approach.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

## Environment

### Establish a Ministry for Animal and Plant Welfare and extend legal advocacy to nature (PPA-09)

**How** (*archive*): Building on Te Urewera's legal personhood and animals' legal recognition as sentient.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

### Build a government-backed renewables industry and prepare to move infrastructure 10 metres above sea level (PPA-11)

**How** (*archive*): Electrify transport, convert sewage and organic waste to biogas and biodiesel, raise eco-housing standards, phase out gas appliances, and redirect foreign aid toward emissions cuts in the Pacific.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

## Health

### Create an independent National Health Board outside the Health Ministry to oversee Te Whatu Ora (PPA-02)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says this would counterbalance political influence on health priorities.

**How** (*archive*): A board of health experts with elected and appointed members, plus co-operative primary and residential care, Māori-for-Māori services and higher taxes on harmful products ring-fenced for health.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

### Legalise cannabis as a health issue and support the End-of-Life Choice Act (PPA-03)

**How** (*archive*): Tax revenue from cannabis would go to health, with research on benefits and harms; the party also lists voluntary vaccination and a review of Covid-era measures for future pandemics.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

## Housing

### Offer state-funded mortgages, a state-owned house-building enterprise and limit home ownership to NZ residents (PPA-04)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says leaving housing to the market 'amounts to a dereliction of duty'.

**How** (*archive*): Also long-term leasing, co-operative housing and co-housing options, and a capital gains tax to curb speculation.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

## Incomes & employment

### Phase out income tax in favour of taxes on production, remove GST from fresh produce and introduce a capital gains tax (PPA-13)

**How** (*archive*): Income tax would become a mechanism capping salaries at a maximum linked to the minimum wage, set by a Wages and Salary Commission.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

## Law, justice & government

### Focus prisons on rehabilitation, education and restorative justice, and end for-profit prisons (PPA-08)

**Why** (*archive*): The party views crime as rooted in social and economic conditions.

**How** (*archive*): Skills training and tikanga Māori in prisons, mental-health services, restorative justice, community reintegration support, and terminating private prison arrangements.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

### Create Social Boards of respected community members to advise local and national government (PPA-14)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says they would moderate lobby groups' influence.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

## Te ao Māori

### Make te reo Māori compulsory in primary and secondary schools, aiming for a bilingual Aotearoa (PPA-05)

**How** (*archive*): Language parity with English, plus full teaching of New Zealand history and the constitutional documents (Te Tiriti and He Whakaputanga).

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

### Entrench the Māori seats in Parliament (PPA-06)

**How** (*archive*): Give the Māori seats the same entrenched protection as general seats.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

### New policies

#### Create a Toi Māori authority to support Māori arts (POL55339)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that Māori identity cannot be separated from Māori art, so supporting Māori art is supporting Māori people. Funding the Māori arts can ensures a future where mātaurange is healthy and ubiquitous throughout New Zealand life.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would would establish a Toi Māori Authority, which would be separate from and equal to Creative New Zealand. The authority would establish a two-year rotational programme where 1000 artists in the mātauranga space receive 30 hours of paid work a week, with a new cohort replacing them after the two years.

Sources: ['Te Pāti Māori announce Toi Māori Authority and artist income programme', 12 October 2026 (accessed 15 October 2026)](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00101/te-pati-maori-announces-toi-maori-authority-and-artist-income-programme.htm?_gl=1%2A1hm4we0%2A_gcl_au%2AMTk4NTg5NzkzNi4xNzg2NDAxNDc5%2A_ga%2AMTA2ODM2Mjg3Mi4xNzg2NDAxNDc5%2A_ga_GGVMM3MB82%2AczE3OTIwMjI5MDgkbzckZzAkdDE3OTIwMjI5MDkkajU5JGwwJGgw); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/te-pati-maori). #### Invest in kōhanga Reo and kura (POL55340)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that kōhanga reo and kura are vital for regenerating te reo Māori, but many are in need of rebuilds or refurbishment and do not have the funds to do so.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would would pass a Te Kōhanga Reo Act which would ensure kōhanga reo have an annual baseline level of funding. The party would invest $20 million in a capital fund for kōhanga reo, while $50 million would be invested in refurbishing or rebuilding kōhanga reo. The party would also invest $250 million a year over five years in kura, for much the same purposes. This party estimates that this policy would cost $1.25 billion over five years for kura, $70 million for kōhanga reo.

Sources: ['Te Pāti Māori backs kohanga reo and kura with long term investment', 6 October 2026 (accessed 15 October 2026)](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00052/te-pati-maori-backs-kohanga-reo-and-kura-with-long-term-investment.htm?_gl=1%2A1ati0d2%2A_gcl_au%2AMTk4NTg5NzkzNi4xNzg2NDAxNDc5%2A_ga%2AMTA2ODM2Mjg3Mi4xNzg2NDAxNDc5%2A_ga_GGVMM3MB82%2AczE3OTIwMjI5MDgkbzckZzEkdDE3OTIwMjM3ODckajQ3JGwwJGgw); [policy.nz party page](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/te-pati-maori). #### Restore Te Ahu o Te Reo Māori (POL55341)

_Added on policy.nz, first seen 28 October 2026._

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that Te Ahu o te Reo, a programme which supported teachers in learning te Reo Māori, was cut by the National-led government. Because of the programme's importance to te reo Māori revitalisation in increasing Māori abilities across the education workforce, this party would restore it.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would bring back and fund Te Ahu o te Reo. This party estimates that this policy would cost $30 million a year.

1. Started from policy.nz's Te Pāti Māori data (`raw/policy.nz/parties/te-pati-maori.json`): statement, Why/How, citations.
2. maoriparty.org.nz blocks automated access (Cloudflare 403, also with a headless browser) and web.archive.org is unreachable from this environment. The party's own web pages were therefore recovered from **Common Crawl**: its 2026 crawl indexes (CC-MAIN-2026-12 … -43) were searched for every maoriparty.org.nz URL and the latest HTTP-200 capture of each page was read from the WARC archive on data.commoncrawl.org (`tools/policies_nzf_tpm_cc_index.py`, `tools/policies_nzf_tpm_cc_fetch.py`). Each such document (`documents/site-*.md`) records the capture date and WARC record; captures date from 2026-03-17 to 2026-10-08, so later edits are not reflected.
3. In addition, every Te Pāti Māori press release and speech from late 2025 to 23 Oct 2026 was collected from Scoop's organisation page (https://info.scoop.co.nz/Te_Pati_Maori); Scoop republishes party releases as issued, so their text is the party's own. Policy PDFs the party attached to releases (img.scoop.co.nz) or linked from its site (Google Drive) were downloaded and text-extracted.
4. Each policy links (a) the page policy.nz cited (now mostly a Common Crawl capture) and (b) other party texts on the same policy. Where a cited page could not be recovered at all, a `documents/not-retrieved-*.md` file records the URL and the reason; it contains no paraphrase.
5. Policies found in party texts but missing from policy.nz were added with neutral summaries (`summary_source: archive`). Calls on the current government and positions (e.g. opposing a bill) are included where the party presents them as what it stands for, and are labelled as such.

## Education & te reo Māori

### POL54679: Create a Māori Education Authority with responsibility for Māori education

**Statement:** Create a Māori Education Authority with responsibility for Māori education  
*Summary source: policy.nz* · topics: te-ao-maori, education, te-reo-maori-and-culture, schools, early-childhood-education

- **Why:** This party says that every child deserves to learn in a way that celebrates their culture. Children who are connected to their identity do better in the education system. Creating education systems that focus on whānau, identity and different knowledge systems will help children to succeed
- **How:** This party would increase funding in kōhanga reo and kura kaupapa Māori, wharekura and wānanga. It would embed the use of mātauranga Māori throughout the curriculum and make te reo Māori a core curriculum subject through Year 10. ### POL54812: Make the first $30,000 earned tax-free

**Statement:** Make the first $30,000 earned tax-free  
*Summary source: policy.nz* · topics: incomes-and-employment, economy, tax-and-income-support, government-revenue-and-finance, wages-and-working-conditions

- **Why:** This party says that argues that Aotearoa's tax system is highly unequal, given that wages are taxed more than income from wealth. Lower-earning people have less disposable income; this party seeks to reduce how much this group is taxed.
- **How:** This party would establish six bands of income tax. The first $30,000 earned would be tax-free, while income between $30,001 and $60,000 would have a tax rate of 15%. Those earning between $60,001 and $90,001 would have a tax rate of 33%; $ 90,001- $ 180,000 would be 39%; between $180,000 and $300,000, 42%; and above $300,000, the tax rate would be 48%.

### POL54802: Establish an independent commissioner for Te Tiriti o Waitangi

### POL54917: Establish an independent Te Tiriti Commission

**Statement:** Establish an independent Te Tiriti Commission  
*Summary source: policy.nz* · topics: te-ao-maori, te-tiriti-o-waitangi-and-governance, te-reo-maori-and-culture

- **Why:** This party says that says that te Triti is the constitutional foundation of Aotearoa, but how te Tiriti is treated depends on the government of the day. Therefore, a crown watchdog regarding the implementation of te Tiriti is required.
- **How:** This party would will create a Te Tiriti commission. The commission would investigate Crown activities which may breach Te Tiriti, report to Parliament on breaches, stop decisions or actions which breach Te Tiriti and require remedial action from the Crown when such breaches occur. The commission would use a Te Tiriti compliance order to prevent the government from continuing the activity. Such orders could only be overturned by the High Court.

### POL54921: Convene a Māori constitutional convention as laid out in Matike Mai

**Statement:** Convene a Māori constitutional convention as laid out in Matike Mai  
*Summary source: policy.nz* · topics: te-ao-maori, law-justice-and-government, te-reo-maori-and-culture, te-tiriti-o-waitangi-and-governance, parliament-and-democracy

- **Why:** This party says that Māori constitutional sovereignty comes from He Whakaputanga o te Rangatiratanga o Nu Tireni (the 1835 declaration of independence). However, with no written constitution, Māori authority is not constitutionally enshrined as it should be. The Mātike Mai project, which was founded in 2010 to strengthen the independence of iwi and hapū, is underfunded to resource such a transition.
- **How:** This party would convene a Māori constitutional convention which will start dialogue with tangata Tiriti and both local and central government regarding New Zealand's constitutional future. It would set 2040 as a target date for constitutional change in New Zealand, and estimates that this policy would cost $220m. This would follow the recommendations of the Matike Mai report.
- **Note:** A 2023 Te Pāti Māori 'Mana Motuhake Policy' PDF is archived for reference (documents/pdf-mana-motuhake-1y9gti2vgayijygamaq5e-wvclylcoytl.md); it predates 2026 and is not cited as 2026 policy.

# Te Tai Tokerau Party — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **Te Tai Tokerau Party** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **22 policies** listed, backed by **1 full-text source document**.

- Party website: <https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/>
- Registration: 5 August 2026 (Electoral Commission register)

## About this list

The Te Tai Tokerau Party was launched by Te Tai Tokerau MP Mariameno Kapa-Kingi in May 2026 after her split from Te Pāti Māori. Its whole platform is published on one page, "TTP Pātaka Policy", organised in five pillars (Whānau, Whare, Whenua, Tino Rangatiratanga, Ōhanga Ā-Rohe). Each named policy on that page is listed below. The page does not give costings except where noted.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/te-tai-tokerau-party/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). Party claims (costs, statistics) are reported as the party's claims, not verified.

**Gaps and caveats.** The "Tai Tokerau Fund" policy is marked by the party as "in development". No separate PDFs, press releases or costings were found on the site.

## Headline policies

- [Pass Te Ture Mokopuna (the Mokopuna Act) requiring government decisions to consider current and future generations of mokopuna](#pass-te-ture-mokopuna-the-mokopuna-act-requiring-government-decisions-to-consider-current-and-future-generations-of-mokopuna-ttp-01) — Community & inclusion
- [Wipe low-income whānau debt to MSD and IRD and replace the benefit system with a Universal Whānau Allowance](#wipe-low-income-whānau-debt-to-msd-and-ird-and-replace-the-benefit-system-with-a-universal-whānau-allowance-ttp-03) — Incomes & employment
- [Constitutionally protect He Whakaputanga and Te Tiriti, and repeal the Regulatory Standards Act 2025 and the Treaty Clauses Review](#constitutionally-protect-he-whakaputanga-and-te-tiriti-and-repeal-the-regulatory-standards-act-2025-and-the-treaty-clauses-review-ttp-13) — Te ao Māori

## Community & inclusion

### Pass Te Ture Mokopuna (the Mokopuna Act) requiring government decisions to consider current and future generations of mokopuna (TTP-01)

**Why** (*archive*): The party calls this its flagship policy, modelled on Wales's Well-being of Future Generations Act 2015 and grounded in mātauranga Māori and Te Tiriti.

**How** (*archive*): Public bodies would be bound by a 'Mokopuna Principle', report annually against mokopuna wellbeing goals, carry out Mokopuna Impact Assessments on significant laws, Budgets and projects, and be monitored by an independent Commissioner for Mokopuna using co-designed national indicators.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Provide free solar power, home-delivered kai and paid cultural roles for kaumātua (TTP-07)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says many kaumātua live in energy poverty and are cut off from whānau and tribal roles.

**How** (*archive*): Prioritise elder-occupied homes for fully funded solar and batteries on community grids with zero-cost baseline electricity; monthly fresh-food prescription vouchers delivered to homes; paid mentorship roles for kaumātua and kuia; and paid, trained in-home carers drawn from local whānau ('Ringa Manaaki Dividend').

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

## Economy

### Build Local Business Incubators in Whangārei, Kaikohe and Kaitaia with a five-year 100% tax holiday for start-ups (TTP-19)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says young people leave the North because it lacks high-spec commercial infrastructure.

**How** (*archive*): Funded co-working spaces with fibre, fabrication labs and studios; businesses based in the incubators would pay no 'regional corporate income tax' for five years if local payroll and staffing targets are met; plus mentoring and seed grants.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Require government agencies to buy 10% (rising to 15% by 2030) of goods and services from Māori-owned and local businesses (TTP-20)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says state money spent in the regions should stay there.

**How** (*archive*): A 'Social & Indigenous Procurement Mandate' for schools, hospitals and construction, a 35% local Māori employment and 50% youth/apprenticeship target on regional projects, and 'Farm to School' purchasing of Māori-grown food.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Create a Tai Tokerau Fund modelled on the Provincial Growth Fund, specific to iwi (details in development) (TTP-22)

**How** (*archive*): The party lists a regional, iwi-specific fund modelled on the Provincial Growth Fund; its page says full detail is still in development.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

## Environment

### Set up a $150m-a-year Kaitiaki Guardians Network with statutory environmental enforcement powers (TTP-09)

**Why** (*archive*): The party wants Māori to move from being 'consulted' on the environment to being its legal 'eyes and ears'.

**How** (*archive*): A $150 million annual Crown appropriation for iwi- and hapū-led guardian teams with statutory power to monitor and enforce environmental rules in their rohe, including issuing protection notices for urupā, marae and biodiversity hotspots.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Create a Whenua Climate Restoration Fund giving iwi first right of refusal to buy back low-lying and coastal land, and a Māori Biodiversity Credit System (TTP-10)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says climate adaptation needs space and that iwi should control ecosystems that buffer against sea-level rise and food insecurity.

**How** (*archive*): A fund backing a compulsory first right of refusal for iwi to buy ecologically significant low-lying and coastal land, and Crown payments to whānau and iwi for carbon sequestration and ecosystem services from restored forests and wetlands.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Make marae official off-grid Civil Defence hubs with funded energy, water, stockpiles and training (TTP-11)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says marae already open their doors in emergencies long before state agencies arrive.

**How** (*archive*): Fund solar, batteries, rainwater collection and filtration at designated marae; stock emergency supplies and satellite communications; and legally designate marae as co-equal Civil Defence hubs under NEMA with funded emergency training for whānau.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Replace marine law with a Moana Ora Act protecting 30% of territorial waters through iwi/hapū-managed areas (TTP-12)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says current marine management is fragmented and ignores customary rights.

**How** (*archive*): Repeal and replace marine legislation with an act mandating Indigenous Protected and Conserved Areas, a binding 30% protection target co-designed and managed by iwi/hapū (including seasonal rāhui), an end to destructive bottom trawling and secured customary fishing rights.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

## Health

### Establish Te Aka Motuhake, a fully iwi-governed Māori health commissioning authority, plus a bonded iwi health scholarship scheme (TTP-05)

**Why** (*archive*): The party rejects the mainstreaming of indigenous health structures and wants to fix the Māori health workforce shortage.

**How** (*archive*): An autonomous, state-funded but iwi-governed health authority controlling clinical design, regional funding and provider licensing; an uncapped scholarship bonding graduates to Māori, iwi or rural providers for at least four years; and more diagnostic, preventative and dental services delivered from tribal hubs.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

## Housing

### Train local rangatahi to build hempcrete homes on papakāinga through a Rohe Construction Academy (TTP-08)

**Why** (*archive*): The party links overcrowded, damp housing to high rates of rheumatic fever and respiratory illness and says imported materials make building expensive.

**How** (*archive*): A funded trade academy in Te Tai Tokerau paying trainees a living wage; regional plants turning local hemp hurd and lime into certified building panels; and homes built on ancestral land and papakāinga, allocated first to overcrowded families and bypassing commercial developers.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

## Incomes & employment

### Wipe low-income whānau debt to MSD and IRD and replace the benefit system with a Universal Whānau Allowance (TTP-03)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says whānau cannot retrain or innovate while being penalised by MSD, and that the current system creates a poverty trap.

**How** (*archive*): An immediate amnesty on about $2 billion of debt owed by low-income whānau to MSD and IRD; a simplified, non-taxable Universal Whānau Allowance for people in training or caregiving; and an end to 'relationship status' policing in the benefit system.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Fund 'Backyard Sovereignty Kits' (garden beds, chickens, rain tanks) and deregulate small-scale local food trade (TTP-06)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says supermarket prices are crippling for Northland whānau and that home food production should be treated as regional infrastructure.

**How** (*archive*): Funded flat-pack kits with raised beds, soil, seeds, a predator-proof coop and laying hens; rain-water catchment and irrigation; mobile gardening mentors; and an exemption of hyper-local household food barter and sales from council licensing and transaction taxes.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Fund community-owned Kai Sovereignty food hubs and require Northland supermarkets to give 30% of shelf space to local produce (TTP-21)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says the supermarket duopoly trucks northern produce to Auckland and back with large markups.

**How** (*archive*): Fund regional processing hubs (kitchens, cold storage, butchery, packing), support direct-to-consumer networks, and require supermarkets in Te Tai Tokerau to allocate at least 30% of shelf space to locally grown unprocessed food bought from regional suppliers.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

## Law, justice & government

### Adopt a 'prison sinking lid' that diverts non-violent offenders with addiction or mental-health needs into hapū-run rehabilitation (TTP-04)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says each prisoner costs over $150,000 a year while reoffending stays high, and that rural communities lack preventative resources.

**How** (*archive*): Corrections savings from each bed vacated through health-focused diversion would be legally transferred to local hapū-led rehabilitation trusts running secure, alcohol- and drug-free 'healing sanctuaries', with mandatory restorative work programmes for those diverted.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Pass a Māori Justice & Autonomous Policing Act transferring youth-justice funding to iwi-governed authorities (TTP-18)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says state-controlled corrections and punitive policing entrench institutional inequity.

**How** (*archive*): Transfer regional youth-justice budgets to iwi-governed, marae-anchored authorities and fund iwi-administered community safety services under tribal jurisdiction, with restorative justice replacing incarceration.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

## Te ao Māori

### Create a Crown–Iwi Investment Fund and give mana whenua a 25% equity stake in major regional infrastructure (TTP-02)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says the state should co-invest in iwi- and hapū-owned assets so whānau become owners in the value chain rather than low-wage labour.

**How** (*archive*): A Crown–Iwi Investment Fund for 'transition infrastructure' (renewable energy, green hydrogen, digital); major regional projects such as wind farms would have to offer at least 25% equity to local mana whenua, funded by low-interest government loans.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Constitutionally protect He Whakaputanga and Te Tiriti, and repeal the Regulatory Standards Act 2025 and the Treaty Clauses Review (TTP-13)

**Why** (*archive*): The party notes that both founding documents were signed in Te Tai Tokerau and wants protection against legislative harm to them.

**How** (*archive*): Advance a Tiriti-centred constitution led by community voices, and, as a priority, vote to repeal the Regulatory Standards Act 2025 and the Treaty Clauses Review.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Increase and entrench Waitangi Tribunal funding and make its findings binding on the Crown beyond specific land types (TTP-14)

**Why** (*archive*): The party sees the Tribunal as a forum for justice relied on by whānau.

**How** (*archive*): Raise and entrench funding (amount to be set after talks with the Tribunal and whānau) and extend the Tribunal's binding jurisdiction over the Crown.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Fund tangata whenua-led Te Tiriti education in the curriculum, the public service and for all MPs (TTP-15)

**How** (*archive*): More funding for Te Tiriti education led by tangata whenua, embedded in the NZ Curriculum and in public-service professional development, including for all sitting MPs.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Redirect 20% of Crown revenue from conservation and public land into a Māori-governed land-buyback fund (TTP-16)

**Why** (*archive*): The party wants to replace lengthy land-return negotiations with automatic, revenue-backed mechanisms.

**How** (*archive*): Legislate a mandatory 20% redirection of Crown revenues from conservation and public lands into a Māori-governed Land Acquisition Fund, remove LINZ's disposal authority and automatically return unused public-works land to its original owners, with a right of first refusal to buy back private land.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Create Te Whare Tohu Tātai, an independent Māori data and Crown-compliance commission (TTP-17)

**How** (*archive*): A statutory commission to monitor Crown compliance with all historical settlements, with ownership and control of all state data about Māori whānau and enforcement powers.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Oppose adding 'gender identity and gender expression' to the Human Rights Act (WRP-03)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says it could undermine sex-based exceptions.

Full text: [POLICY – Human Rights Act – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-human-rights-act.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/human-rights-act/)); [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx))

### Remove 'gender, gender identity and gender expression' from the Conversion Practices Prohibition Act (WRP-04)

**Why** (*archive*): It supports protecting lesbian, gay and bisexual people from conversion practices but says 'gender' is not a clear concept for law.

Full text: [Conversion Practices – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-conversion-practices.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/conversion-practices/)); [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx))

### Keep commercial surrogacy illegal, ban international surrogacy by New Zealanders and lengthen the birth mother's decision period (WRP-07)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says surrogacy cannot be free of exploitation and having a baby by surrogacy is not a human right.

**How** (*archive*): Keep the birth mother as first legal parent with longer than seven days to decide; children should be able to learn their origins.

Full text: [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx))

### Protect single-sex spaces and keep biological males out of women's prisons (WRP-09)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says women's rights must be based on biological sex rather than gender identity.

**How** (*archive*): Single-sex toilets, changing rooms, refuges, wards, sports and women-only groups (including online); school privacy from the opposite sex; supportive conditions for pregnant prisoners and mothers.

Full text: [Protecting Women’s and Children’s Spaces and Safety – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-exit-services-for-women-leaving-gangs-religious-cults-and-se.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/exit-services-for-women-leaving-gangs-religious-cults-and-services-to-support-detransitioners/)); [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx))

### Fund women-only refuges, exit services for women leaving gangs or cults, and support for detransitioners (WRP-10)

**How** (*archive*): More resources to leave domestic violence and accessible, affordable, enforced protection orders.

Full text: [Protecting Women’s and Children’s Spaces and Safety – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-exit-services-for-women-leaving-gangs-religious-cults-and-se.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/exit-services-for-women-leaving-gangs-religious-cults-and-services-to-support-detransitioners/))

### Use language in law, health and education that defines women as adult human females and motherhood as exclusively female (WRP-17)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says women's rights must be based on biological sex rather than gender identity.

**How** (*archive*): Keep words such as 'mother', 'woman' and 'breastfeeding' in maternity services.

Full text: [Our Priorities](documents/our-priorities.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/our-priorities/)); [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx)); [Advocating for Women – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-advocating-for-women.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/advocating-for-women/))

## Defence & foreign affairs

### Stand with women denied education, work and safety worldwide (WRP-16)

**How** (*archive*): Its international policy statement.

Full text: [International – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-international.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/international/))

## Education

### Require parents to be told what is taught in sexuality education and stop schools supporting 'social transition' (WRP-11)

**Why** (*archive*): The party broadly supports the new RSE Framework because it recognises biological sex.

**How** (*archive*): Full disclosure to parents, no outside agencies such as InsideOut, teach that under-16s cannot consent, refer distressed children to professionals with parents involved.

Full text: [Policy — Educating our Young People – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-educating-our-young-people.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/educating-our-young-people/)); [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx))

## Environment

### Add a principle of the right to a clean and safe natural environment (WRP-15)

Full text: [Environmental – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-environmental.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/environmental/))

## Health

### Ban puberty blockers and cross-sex hormones for under-18s with 'sex-related distress' and restrict funded gender surgery to over-25s (WRP-01)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says women's rights must be based on biological sex rather than gender identity.

**How** (*archive*): Also an inquiry into Health NZ's contracting of PATHA to write gender-affirming care guidelines, which it notes scored poorly in the Cass Report assessment.

Full text: [Puberty blockers, hormones and surgery – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-puberty-blockers-hormones-and-surgery.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/puberty-blockers-hormones-and-surgery/)); [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx))

## Incomes & employment

### Extend paid parental leave from six to 12 months, reform Working for Families and fund continuity of midwifery care (WRP-12)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says mothering and caring is work that contributes to society.

**How** (*archive*): Partner leave in addition to the mother's, CPAG-style WFF reform removing discrimination against beneficiary families, wrap-around support for vulnerable mothers, free or affordable childcare and a review of for-profit ECE.

Full text: [Caring for Mothers and Children – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-working-for-families-reform.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/working-for-families-reform/)); [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx))

### Deliver pay equity in the public and private sectors and reinstate Fair Pay Agreements (WRP-13)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says about 150,000 women's pay-equity claims were extinguished by the 2025 law change.

**How** (*archive*): A strong onus on employers and publication of average hourly pay by occupation, sex and ethnicity.

Full text: [Pay equity – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-pay-equity.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/pay-equity/)); [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx))

### Raise minimum wages and benefits and provide free financial advice to secure older women's incomes (WRP-14)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says older women are the fastest-growing group in poverty globally.

**How** (*archive*): Living incomes, affordable housing and work with the Office for Seniors on solutions to the retirement savings gap.

Full text: [Financial Stability for Women in Older Age – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-financial-stability-for-women-in-older-age.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/financial-stability-for-women-in-older-age/)); [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx))

## Law, justice & government

### Replace the Prostitution Reform Act with the 'Nordic' Equality Model criminalising buyers and brothel owners (WRP-05)

**How** (*archive*): Decriminalise the prostituted person, criminalise exploiters, fund exit services; meanwhile keep section 19 (barring temporary-visa holders from sex work) to deter trafficking.

Full text: [Prostitution Reform – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-prostitution.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/prostitution/)); [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx))

### Ban the 'rough sex' defence in murder and serious-harm cases (WRP-06)

**Why** (*archive*): The party opposes pornography involving strangulation and violence.

Full text: [“Rough Sex” murder defence – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-rough-sex-murder-defence.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/rough-sex-murder-defence/)); [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx))

### Add 'sex' to the Sentencing Act's aggravating factors instead of creating new hate-crime laws (WRP-08)

**How** (*archive*): Amend section 9(1)(h) to include sex, oppose 'gender identity' as an aggravating factor and oppose new hate-crime offences.

Full text: [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx))
